brief_summary:
This multicenter, open-label, prospective, randomized controlled study compares a novel endoscopy-assisted breast-conserving surgery technique (SRRSHzb-EABCS) with conventional open breast-conserving surgery (CBCS) in women with breast cancer who wish to preserve their breast.

Breast-conserving surgery followed by radiotherapy is a standard treatment for early-stage breast cancer. Conventional open surgery leaves visible scars on the breast, while traditional endoscopy-assisted techniques are time-consuming, difficult to learn, and costly. The investigators developed a novel technique, SRRSHzb-EABCS, which uses a gasless expansion-traction endoscopic system with a custom-built skin flap dissector and V-shaped retractor, together with percutaneous U-shaped metal wires placed around the marked tumor margin, enabling precise tumor localization and margin control through a single axillary incision. The technique is designed to be easier to learn, shorter in operative time, less expensive, and more cosmetic.

Eligible participants are randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo either SRRSHzb-EABCS or conventional open breast-conserving surgery. The main goal of the study is to compare the intraoperative and postoperative positive margin rates between the two techniques. The study also compares aesthetic outcomes measured by BREAST-Q scores at 1 and 18 months after surgery, complication rates, and 5-year local recurrence, disease-free survival, and overall survival.

A total of 422 participants (211 per arm) will be enrolled at Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, and multiple participating centers in China. Participants are followed at 1 month and 18 months after surgery, with long-term follow-up for up to 5 years.
primary_outcomes: Intraoperative and Postoperative Positive Margin Rate
title: Comparison of the Safety and Aesthetic Outcomes of a Novel Endoscopic-Assisted Breast-Conserving Surgery (SRRSHzb-EABCS) With Those of Conventional Breast-Conserving Surgery

brief_summary:
This study was aimed to investigate the effects of pre-operative nutritional status and post-operative dietary interventions on inflammation, pain, and recovery in adults undergoing lumbar disc surgery.

Participants were planned to undergo nutritional assessment before surgery and receive either an individualized anti-inflammatory diet or a standard balanced diet after surgery. Dietary intake was monitored over a four-week postoperative period.

The study evaluated whether an anti-inflammatory dietary intervention can reduce postoperative inflammation, pain, and complications compared with a standard diet. It also examined the relationship between pre-operative nutritional status and post-operative recovery of the patients.

The findings may help improve nutritional assessment and dietary management in patients undergoing lumbar disc surgery.
primary_outcomes: Change in Chromogranin A (CgA) Levels
title: Effects of an Anti-Inflammatory Diet on Inflammatory and Neuroendocrine Responses After Lumbar Discectomy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding virtual reality (VR) training to conventional rehabilitation improves arm movement in adults who had a stroke 6 to 24 months earlier, and whether VR training 5 days a week gives more benefit than VR training 2 days a week. The study will also measure three blood markers that may reflect brain and muscle adaptation (BDNF, irisin and S100B).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does arm motor function, measured with the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity 12 weeks after the start of treatment, improve more when VR training is added to conventional rehabilitation, and does it improve more with 5 than with 2 VR sessions a week?
* As an exploratory question, do blood levels of BDNF, irisin and S100B change differently between the groups, and are these changes related to the improvement in arm function?

Researchers will compare three groups: conventional rehabilitation alone, conventional rehabilitation plus VR training 2 days a week, and conventional rehabilitation plus VR training 5 days a week.

Participants will:

* Be assigned by chance to one of the three groups
* Receive conventional rehabilitation for 45 minutes, 5 days a week, for 4 weeks; depending on their group, they will also receive 30-minute VR sessions with the Neuroforma system 2 or 5 days a week
* Follow a home exercise program from week 4 to week 12
* Have arm function tests and a fasting morning blood sample at the start of the study, at week 4 and at week 12
primary_outcomes: Change in Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) Motor Score From Baseline to Week 12
title: Virtual Reality Training Dose for Arm Recovery After Stroke: Clinical and Blood Biomarker Responses

brief_summary:
During laparoscopic surgery, the abdomen is inflated with carbon dioxide gas (pneumoperitoneum), which alters venous return and fluid distribution, potentially leading to swelling in the tissues of the upper airway. The placement of a breathing tube (endotracheal tube) under general anesthesia can also cause local airway irritation and edema. Although these airway dimension changes are frequently clinically silent, they can be accurately visualized and quantified at the bedside using non-invasive ultrasonography.

Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid with potent anti-inflammatory and anti-edematous actions commonly administered before surgery to alleviate postoperative nausea, vomiting, and sore throat. However, whether it helps prevent or attenuate measurable increases in airway wall thickness during and after laparoscopic surgery remains unclear.

The primary purpose of this randomized clinical trial is to evaluate whether a single preventive intravenous dose of dexamethasone attenuates upper-airway swelling, measured primarily by lateral pharyngeal wall thickness via ultrasound, in adult patients undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

Participants are randomly allocated into one of two groups:

* Dexamethasone Group: Receives an intravenous dose of dexamethasone (0.2 mg/kg) diluted in 10 mL normal saline prior to the induction of general anesthesia.
* Placebo Group: Receives an identical volume of 10 mL normal saline intravenously prior to the induction of general anesthesia.

Bedside ultrasound scans will be performed by a blinded assessor to evaluate lateral pharyngeal wall thickness, tongue thickness, and parapharyngeal space dimensions at five specific time points: before anesthesia induction, 30 minutes following pneumoperitoneum initiation, immediately prior to extubation, 1 hour after extubation, and 2 hours after extubation. Participants are also evaluated for any post-extubation airway complications or symptoms during their stay in the recovery unit.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Total Bilateral Lateral Pharyngeal Wall (LPW) Thickness at Pre-extubation
title: Effect of Prophylactic Dexamethasone vs Placebo on Airway Dimensions Assessed by Ultrasonography in Patients Undergoing Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy

brief_summary: This will be an open-label, single-arm, prospective study, in which patients requiring RT for locally and/or regionally advanced head and neck cancers will undergo a combination treatment comprised of intravenously delivered PROMITIL and standard-of-care radiotherapy (RT). The treatment regimen will involve administration of 3 PROMITIL doses, delivered at 21-day intervals, and a course of external beam radiotherapy (EBR), initiated 1-3 days after the first PROMITIL dose. EBR will consist of either standard daily fractionation (5 per week) of up to a total of 70 Gy at 2 Gy/fraction (7 weeks) or a hypofractionated regimen of up to 55 Gy at 2.75 Gy/fraction (HYPNO regimen; 4 weeks), per investigator's preference. PROMITIL will be given by intravenous infusion at a dose of 2 mg/kg body weight with a capped maximal dose of 150 mg. Five sentinel patients (the first five enrolled patients) will be treated with a dose of 1.8 mg/kg body weight for the purpose of conducting a safety analysis to determine tolerability of the dosing regimen prior to enrolling the remaining study patients. Treatment safety will be assessed on a weekly basis, as well as 4 weeks after the last RT treatment. Disease status will be reevaluated 28 days (±7 days) from the end of last radiation treatment by a direct clinical examination. PET CT or CT will be conducted 12 weeks (±7 days) from the end of RT treatment. Thereafter, PET CT and/or CT scans will be repeated every 6 months for the first 24 months, followed by yearly imaging. In addition, during the follow-up phase, the patient will be assessed by a radiation oncologist and/or ENT specialist every 3 months during the first year, every 4 months during the second and third years and every 6 months in years 4 and 5 of observation. A first interim analysis will be conducted 3 months after end of treatment to evaluate safety and response rate. A second interim analysis will be conducted 2 years after end of treatment to evaluate event-free survival (EFS) and delayed toxicities. Final analysis of long-term disease control and survival will be conducted after 5 years.
conditions: Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
interventions: Addition of Promitil to External Beam Radiotherapy
primary_outcomes: Short and Intermediate-Term Safety
2-year event-free survival (EFS)
title: Intravenously Administered PROMITIL Combined With Radiotherapy in Patients With Cisplatin-Ineligible Head and Neck Cancer Patients

brief_summary:
This prospective, randomized, sham-controlled clinical trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness of pulsed electromagnetic field (PEMF) therapy in patients with symptomatic plantar calcaneal spurs. A total of 100 participants will be randomly assigned to either an active PEMF group or a sham PEMF group in a 1:1 ratio. Both groups will receive a standardized stretching exercise program.

The primary outcome will be the change in morning first-step pain intensity. Secondary outcomes will include foot function assessed using the Foot Function Index (FFI), plantar fascia thickness measured by ultrasonography, and pressure pain threshold measured using an algometer. Assessments will be performed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, and 12 to evaluate the short- and medium-term effects of PEMF therapy.

brief_summary:
Pulmonary sarcoidosis may be accompanied by obstructive ventilatory defects and bronchial hyperresponsiveness (BHR), which can mimic the clinical presentation of asthma. In clinical practice, bronchial challenge tests are used as an adjunctive tool in the diagnosis of asthma in patients with suggestive symptoms but normal spirometry results. However, BHR is not specific to asthma and is also observed in patients with sarcoidosis. Further research is warranted by reports suggesting an association between BHR and the severity of respiratory symptoms in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis. To assess the prevalence of BHR in the course of sarcoidosis and identify factors associated with its occurrence, methacholine bronchial challenge tests were performed in patients with sarcoidosis.

Despite the existing hypotheses explaining the presence of bronchial hyperresponsiveness in sarcoidosis, its pathogenesis remains largely unknown. The use of a methacholine bronchial challenge test and the assessment of its association with pulmonary radiological findings may help identify patients with sarcoidosis who are at increased risk of bronchial hyperresponsiveness, as well as improve our understanding of the mechanisms underlying its development.
lead_sponsor: Bydgoszcz University of Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of bronchial hyperresponsiveness in patients with sarcoidosis
title: Bronchial Hyperresponsiveness in Sarcoidosis

brief_summary:

Researchers will compare FRAME to a waitlist group (participants who receive the programme after the study ends) to see if FRAME makes a difference.

Participants will:

* Attend six weekly 2-hour group sessions, each combining mind-body practices and family resilience concepts
* Practise mindfulness exercises at home between sessions
* Complete questionnaires before and immediately after the programme, and 3 months later

brief_summary: Pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain is one of the most frequent musculoskeletal complications of pregnancy and the postpartum period. Its prevalence during pregnancy ranges between 20% and 70%, and about 10% of women still have symptoms beyond three months after delivery (persistent postpartum pelvic girdle pain). It limits walking, stair-climbing, prolonged standing, lifting and turning in bed, just when the demands of caring for a newborn are highest. Hypopressive exercise combines diaphragmatic apnea with a costal expansion manoeuvre to co-activate the transversus abdominis and pelvic floor muscles, core stabilization restores lumbopelvic neuromuscular control, and whole-body vibration (WBV) enhances recruitment of trunk and pelvic stabilizers. However, the combination of these approaches has not yet been investigated in postpartum pelvic girdle pain. This randomized clinical trial will compare hypopressive-core stabilization with WBV (Group A) against hypopressive-core stabilization alone (Group B) on pain, mobility and disability. Thirty postpartum women (15 per group) will be recruited by convenient sampling from physiotherapy centers in Lahore and randomly allocated using sealed opaque envelopes. Both groups will attend 3 supervised sessions per week for a total of 8 weeks (24 sessions), each preceded by a moist hot pack for 15 minutes. Each session combines progressive hypopressive postures with core stabilization exercises (squats, bridge and push-up positions); in Group A the core exercises are performed on a vibrating platform at 25 Hz and 2 mm amplitude. Pain (NPRS), pelvic girdle disability (PGQ) and functional mobility (Timed Up and Go) will be measured by a blinded assessor at baseline, end of week 4 and end of week 8. The whole study will be completed within 8 months after synopsis approval. The findings can assist physiotherapists in implementing evidence-based treatment strategies and contribute to better maternal health outcomes for postpartum women.
interventions: Hypopressive-core stabilization exercises combined with whole-body vibration
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS)
Pelvic Girdle Questionnaire (PGQ)
Timed Up and Go (TUG) test
title: Hypopressive-Core Stabilization With and Without Whole-Body Vibration in Postpartum Pelvic Girdle Pain

brief_summary: Low bone mineral density after menopause increases the risk of osteoporosis and fractures, and regular exercise can help preserve bone health. However, adherence to home exercise programs is often low. This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate whether an artificial intelligence-supported mobile health application improves the effects of a home exercise program in postmenopausal women with osteopenia. Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups. Both groups will perform the same 6-month home-based bodyweight strengthening and high-impact exercise program three times per week, using a printed exercise booklet and an exercise adherence log; one group will perform the same exercise program using the mobile application. Bone mineral density, functional status, fall risk, quality of life, and active participation as reflected by exercise adherence will be compared between the groups at baseline and after 6 months.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Lumbar Spine (L1-L4) Bone Mineral Density
title: AI-Supported Mobile High-Impact and Strengthening Exercise Program in Postmenopausal Women With Low Bone Density

brief_summary:
Mitochondrial cytopathies are a heterogeneous group of rare inherited diseases characterized by primary mitochondrial dysfunction caused by a pathogenic mutation located either in nuclear DNA or mitochondrial DNA. Mitochondrial cytopathies can virtually begin at any age, affect any tissue or organ, and involve all modes of inheritance (autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, maternal, etc.).

Muscle stem cells are highly specialized cells that enable skeletal muscle repair after injury. Upon activation, these cells proliferate, differentiate, and fuse to repair damaged muscle fibers. The process by which a myocyte (a differentiated, mononucleated muscle stem cell) fuses with a muscle fiber (i.e., a myofiber) is called myonuclear accretion.

Through work conducted in the investigators' laboratory using preclinical models (cell lines and mouse models), the role of the AMPKα2 signaling pathway in myonuclear accretion has been demonstrated. However, the AMPK pathway is a key regulator of mitochondrial metabolism. The investigators aim to use muscle stem cells derived from muscle biopsies of patients with mitochondrial cytopathies as a model of primary mitochondrial metabolic dysregulation. It is hypothesized that muscle stem cells from these patients exhibit a defect in myonuclear accretion secondary to dysregulation of the AMPKα2 pathway.

Assessing the role of AMPKα2 signaling in the regulation of myonuclear accretion will make it possible to demonstrate that mitochondrial myopathies are not solely a primary pathology of the muscle fiber, but also involve defects in muscle stem cells and in stem cell-myofiber communication. This leads to impaired myonuclear accretion and, ultimately, defective skeletal muscle repair.

This study could open new therapeutic avenues (e.g., pharmacological AMPK activators) for patients with mitochondrial cytopathies, as well as for diseases associated with metabolic dysfunction of muscle stem cells (such as diabetes, obesity, etc.).
primary_outcomes: Metabolic dysfunction
title: Role of AMPKalpha2 in Myonuclear Accretion in Mitochondrial Myopathies

brief_summary:
This is a single-center, prospective observational study of patients with moderate-to-advanced primary Parkinson's disease (PD). PD is the second most common neurodegenerative disease. Current clinical evaluation mainly depends on motor symptoms, and there is a lack of quantitative biomarkers that can dynamically show nigrostriatal neurodegeneration.

This study aims to explore the changing pattern of neurodegeneration by combining ¹⁸F-DOPA PET imaging and blood biomarkers such as neurofilament light chain, alpha-synuclein, GFAP, Tau and inflammatory factors. Thirty-six eligible participants will be enrolled. At baseline, clinical scales, lab tests, blood collection and ¹⁸F-DOPA PET-CT will be performed. Follow-up assessments will take place at 6 and 12 months.

The primary outcome is the change in ¹⁸F-DOPA PET measurements from baseline to 12 months. Secondary outcomes include changes in clinical rating scales and blood biomarkers over 1 year. Participants can receive standardized medication advice for PD during the study.
interventions: Clinical assessment, blood sampling and brain PET examination
primary_outcomes: Change in Putamen 18F-DOPA PET Specific Binding Ratio (SBR) from Baseline to 12 Months
title: Longitudinal Observation of Neurodegeneration in Parkinson's Disease Using Molecular Imaging and Blood Biomarkers

brief_summary: This is a prospective, single-center, observational cohort study that plans to enroll 100 women aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed cervical cancer who are scheduled to receive radical surgery, radiotherapy, or systemic therapy. The study aims to establish and validate a low-depth cfDNA fragmentomics approach-including tumor fraction, fragment length distribution, and copy number variation-together with cfHPV-DNA testing for monitoring recurrence risk and predicting treatment response. Serial blood samples (10 mL per collection) will be obtained before initial treatment, 1-4 weeks after standardized treatment, at 3 and 6 months, and every 3 months thereafter until 2 years after treatment completion or until an endpoint event; fresh or paraffin-embedded tumor tissue will also be collected for whole-exome sequencing and multi-omics analysis. The study will not alter participants' routine clinical treatment. Research-related risks are mainly blood draw-related discomfort, bleeding, or bruising; risks from standard radiotherapy, chemotherapy, or immunotherapy are part of routine clinical care and are not introduced by this observational study. Privacy and confidentiality risks will be minimized through informed consent, secure data storage, restricted database access, and confidential handling of records. cfDNA testing will be provided free of charge, and appropriate compensation may be provided based on participation and time commitment. The study is funded by 3D Medicines (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.; conflict-of-interest, data/sample-sharing, and intellectual property arrangements will be disclosed and managed according to institutional requirements.
primary_outcomes: Objective response rate
title: Use of cfDNA in Monitoring and Guiding Treatment for Cervical Cancer

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled study evaluated the effect of Glo Germ-based visual feedback on surgical hand antisepsis performance among undergraduate nursing students.

A total of 46 third-year nursing students enrolled in an Operating Room Nursing course were randomly assigned to an intervention group (n=23) or a control group (n=23). Both groups received theoretical instruction and conventional practical training in surgical hand antisepsis. In addition, the intervention group received individualized visual feedback using Glo Germ fluorescent training lotion and ultraviolet light to identify areas requiring improvement in hand antisepsis technique.

The primary outcome was surgical hand antisepsis skill performance. Secondary outcomes included knowledge of surgical hand antisepsis and anatomical hand cleanliness. Outcomes were evaluated at the designated assessment points, including a one-month follow-up.

The study aimed to determine whether incorporating fluorescence-based visual feedback into conventional training improves surgical hand antisepsis education among nursing students.
primary_outcomes: Surgical Hand Antisepsis Skill Performance
title: Effect of Glo Germ Visual Feedback on Surgical Hand Antisepsis in Nursing Students

brief_summary: Adolescents with intellectual disabilities (ID) face significant health issues, particularly in managing chronic conditions such as cardiovascular (CV) health risks. These issues are exacerbated by limited physical activity (PA), health literacy challenges, and a lack of evidence-based health interventions. This project aims to address these gaps by engaging adolescents with ID and their stakeholders supporting ID as co-researchers to design, adapt, and pilot-test a virtual reality (VR)-based PA intervention tailored to their needs. The long-term goal is to dismantle factors to improve health outcomes for adolescents with ID through innovative, collaborative research that enhances health literacy, increases PA, and lowers CV health risks. The objectives of this study will address three specific aims: 1) adapt and validate research instruments by collaborating with adolescents with ID and their ID stakeholders to incorporate common language in measures for assessing health outcomes; 2) evaluate and select VR-based PA programs by engaging co-researchers in identifying effective VR exergame interventions for improving health outcomes through PA; and 3) pilot-test the VR PA intervention, which incorporates peer support. We will assess feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of our 16-week VR exergame PA intervention using co-adapted measures and biologic CV risk measures. A quasi-experimental mixed-methods approach will be used, guided by our Logic Model. Preliminary evidence highlights the potential of interactive, technology-driven PA to address CV risks while fostering peer engagement and optimal self-efficacy to manage health. The expected outcomes are: 1) validated measures through greater health literacy, and 2) a co-designed intervention to reduce CV risks that helps adolescents with ID to take an active role in their health. By addressing critical gaps in health literacy, self-efficacy, and PA, this work advances healthcare practices and supports long-term improvements in public health.
interventions: Virtual reality physical activity health promotion intervention
primary_outcomes: Physical Activity
title: Advancing Cardiovascular Health Among Adolescents With Intellectual Disabilities: Co-Development of Technology Interventions to Enhance Physical Activity

brief_summary:
Background Vetting and assigning of protocols to MRI scan requests are usually carried out by radiologists and radiographers. This way is both time-consuming and prone to error. Recent improvements in Artificial Intelligence (Al) like Large Language Models (LLMs) are better at processing human language. It could be used to improve tasks like image reporting and assigning protocols in radiology.

Approach Firstly, I will find out about the delays in the way this is currently done. I will use a survey to find out the perceptions of radiologists to both the current process and the proposed Al intervention.

I will then use an LLM to undertake referral and protocol tasks. I will compare its performance to the performance of clinical specialists and established guidelines.

I will present the explanation reports to radiologists and ask them if they can be understood and whether they can be trusted as clinically reliable.

Impact My research could help reduce the workload and time radiologists spend dealing with scan requests. The findings will help design future research to consider application in real clinical settings.
conditions: Analysis of Retrospectively Collected MRI Referral Data
primary_outcomes: Accuracy
title: Automated Vetting and Protocolling of MRI Examinations

Group A will receive square-stepping exercises with sensory perturbation for 30 minutes, 3 sessions per week for 6 weeks. brief_summary: This is a single-center, single-arm, prospective, Phase II clinical study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of zemetostat combined with anlotinib in patients with head-and-neck soft-tissue sarcoma featuring SWI/SNF complex deficiency whose disease has progressed following standard-of-care therapy. Enrolled patients receive zemetostat plus anlotinib until discontinuation criteria are met. The specific dosing regimen is as follows: zemetostat 350 mg orally twice daily (bid po). The recommended dose of anlotinib is 12 mg once daily for 14 consecutive days, followed by a 7-day drug-free interval (2/1 schedule), constituting a 21-day treatment cycle. Doses should be taken at approximately the same time each day. If a patient vomits or misses a dose, no supplemental dose should be administered on that day; the subsequent scheduled dose should be taken as usual.

brief_summary:
Shoulder arthroscopy is a common outpatient procedure that can cause moderate to severe pain during the first 24 to 48 hours after surgery. An interscalene brachial plexus block (ISB) is widely used to provide pain relief, but it frequently causes temporary weakness or paralysis of the diaphragm (the main breathing muscle) by blocking the phrenic nerve, which can lead to shortness of breath. A combined costoclavicular and suprascapular nerve block (CCB-SSNB) has emerged as an alternative approach that numbs the shoulder while potentially preserving normal breathing and diaphragmatic function. Additionally, adding magnesium sulfate as an adjuvant medication to local anesthetics can help prolong and enhance pain relief.

The primary purpose of this study is to compare the pain-relieving efficacy and respiratory safety of ultrasound-guided combined CCB-SSNB versus standard ISB, both administered with magnesium sulfate as an adjuvant, in adult patients undergoing elective outpatient shoulder arthroscopy under general anesthesia.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups prior to surgery:

* Group A (Combined CCB-SSNB): Participants will receive an ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block (10 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine with 100 mg magnesium sulfate) and an ultrasound-guided costoclavicular block (10 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine with 100 mg magnesium sulfate).
* Group B (ISB): Participants will receive an ultrasound-guided interscalene block (20 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine with 200 mg magnesium sulfate).

The primary outcome is the duration of pain relief, measured as the time from the end of surgery until the patient first requests rescue pain medication. Secondary outcomes include total opioid consumption during the first 24 hours postoperatively, pain scores at rest and during movement up to 48 hours, ultrasound evaluation of diaphragmatic movement to detect hemidiaphragmatic paresis, recovery time in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU), patient satisfaction, and any block-related side effects or complications.
interventions: Combined Costoclavicular and Suprascapular Nerve Block with Magnesium Sulfate
Interscalene Brachial Plexus Block with Magnesium Sulfate
primary_outcomes: Time to First Postoperative Rescue Analgesic Request
title: Magnesium Sulphate as an Adjuvant in Combined Costoclavicular Block and Suprascapular Block Versus Interscalene Block for Ambulatory Shoulder Arthroscopy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if fractional CO₂ laser (FCO₂) with and without intradermal Botulinum Toxin A can treat inflammatory facial acne vulgaris in adult patients of both genders. It will also learn about the safety and tolerability of fractional CO₂ laser (FCO₂) with and without intradermal Botulinum Toxin A in patients with inflammatory facial acne vulgaris.

The main questions it aims to answer is:

* Does fractional CO₂ laser (FCO₂) work effectively in inflammatory facial acne vulgaris?
* is fractional CO₂ laser (FCO₂) well tolerated in inflammatory facial acne vulgaris?
* Is fractional CO₂ laser (FCO₂) monotherapy comparable to fractional CO₂ laser (FCO₂) combined with intradermal Botulinum Toxin A in terms of efficacy and safety in inflammatory facial acne vulgaris?

Researchers will compare fractional CO₂ laser (FCO₂) monotherapy to fractional CO₂ laser (FCO₂) combined with intradermal Botulinum Toxin A to see if crisaborole works as effective and is as well-tolerated in inflammatory facial acne vulgaris.

Participants will:

* Visit the Dermatology clinic to undergo a single session of intradermal Botulinum Toxin A injection to one randomized hemi-face.

  * Then 2 weeks later, they will visit the Dermatology LASER clinic to start fractional CO₂ laser (FCO₂) sessions every 4 weeks, also for checkups and photography.
  * They will receive a total of 3 FCO₂ LASER sessions (4 weeks apart).
  * Then 12 weeks after the last session, they will visit the clinic for follow up, photography and documentation.
* Keep a diary of their symptoms
primary_outcomes: Percentage change in lesion count
Global Acne Grading System (GAGS)
title: Evaluation of the Efficacy and Safety of Fractional CO₂ Laser With and Without Intradermal Botulinum Toxin A in the Treatment of Inflammatory Facial Acne Vulgaris.

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to evaluate whether a targeted regional anesthesia strategy combining an adductor canal block, a nerve to the vastus medialis (NVM) block, an anterior obturator nerve branch block, and an iPACK block improves postoperative recovery in patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction using a hamstring tendon (semitendinosus and gracilis; DIDT) graft, compared with the standard analgesic protocol used in participating centres, consisting of a femoral nerve block combined with an iPACK block.

The main question the study aims to answer is whether this targeted combination of nerve blocks, compared with the standard femoral nerve block plus iPACK regimen, improves the quality of postoperative recovery, as measured by the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at 24 hours after surgery.

The study hypothesis is that the targeted adductor canal + NVM + anterior obturator branch + iPACK strategy will significantly improve postoperative recovery quality at 24 hours compared with the standard femoral nerve block + iPACK protocol, with an expected improvement of at least 8 points on the QoR-15 score. This 8-point difference represents the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for this questionnaire (Léger et al., 2020). The QoR-15 is a validated global recovery assessment tool, available in French, and sensitive to variations in recovery quality in outpatient orthopedic surgery (Nakase et al., 2021). An improvement of at least 8 points at 24 hours would therefore indicate a clinically meaningful benefit from the patient's perspective.

The study will also assess:

* Postoperative pain at rest and during mobilization.
* Opioid consumption during the first 48 hours after surgery.
* Incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting.
* Time to first ambulation.
* Postoperative thigh edema.
* Neuromuscular recovery of the thigh.
* Patient satisfaction with analgesic management.
* Adverse events related to regional anesthesia.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups. All participants will undergo ACL reconstruction with a DIDT graft. Participants in the comparator group will receive a femoral nerve block combined with an iPACK block. Participants in the intervention group will receive a targeted regional anesthesia strategy combining an adductor canal block, a nerve to the vastus medialis (NVM) block, an anterior branch of the obturator nerve block, and an iPACK block.

Postoperative assessments will include pain scores, QoR-15 questionnaires, opioid consumption, nausea and vomiting, thigh measurements, and neuromuscular function assessments during the first 48 hours after surgery. Patient satisfaction and safety outcomes will also be assessed during follow-up.

The primary outcome will compare the QoR-15 score at 24 hours between the two groups, with an 8-point difference considered clinically meaningful.
lead_sponsor: GCS Ramsay Santé pour l'Enseignement et la Recherche
primary_outcomes: Quality of Recovery (QoR-15) Score
title: Nerve Block of the Vastus Medialis and Anterior Obturator Branch in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction With DIDT Graft

brief_summary:
Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common musculoskeletal condition associated with pain, impaired physical function, and movement-related fear. Psychological factors, particularly fear of movement (kinesiophobia), may influence movement behavior and limit participation in physical activity and exercise therapy. Immersive virtual reality (VR) provides an opportunity to modify the visual environment and potentially influence how individuals perceive safety and threat during movement. However, it remains unclear how VR-induced perceptions of safety and fear affect gait biomechanics, particularly in individuals with KOA.

The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of immersive VR environments designed to promote safety or induce fear on gait biomechanics and psychological responses in individuals with KOA and healthy adults aged 50 years and older.

Participants will perform walking tasks under five experimental conditions: walking without VR, walking in a neutral VR environment, walking in a safety-promoting VR environment on low ground, walking in a fear-inducing VR environment, and walking in a safety-promoting VR environment on high ground.

During each condition, participants will walk along a straight 6-meter walkway at their preferred comfortable speed. Gait biomechanics will be assessed using an inertial motion capture system and force platforms. The primary outcome will be gait speed. Additional biomechanical parameters and subjective responses, including perceived fear, safety, and VR-related experiences, will also be assessed.

The study aims to determine whether VR environments that alter perceived safety and fear influence walking patterns and whether these responses differ between individuals with KOA and healthy adults. It is hypothesized that fear-inducing VR environments will alter gait biomechanics, particularly gait speed, compared with neutral and safety-promoting conditions.
primary_outcomes: Gait Speed
title: Effects of Virtual Reality Environments on Walking in Adults With and Without Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary: Infection prevention and control programs at US hospitals perform surveillance to detect and publicly report hospital-onset central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI) using standards set by CDC's National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN). Because this process requires time-consuming review of the medical record by dedicated infection preventionists, VA has developed a generative artificial intelligence (AI) tool that applies the NHSN CLABSI standard to clinical data from the medical record. In this quality improvement initiative, we will evaluate the tool as it is implemented operationally across a cohort of VA medical centers in 3 randomized waves. The purpose of this evaluation is (1) to determine whether the tool reduces the time required for CLABSI surveillance, (2) to assess the objectivity and trustworthiness of the tool from the perspective of infection preventionists, and (3) to detect patient safety events.
interventions: Generative AI tool for CLABSI surveillance
primary_outcomes: Time per bacteremia case review
title: Evaluation of an AI-Assisted Tool for CLABSI Surveillance at VA Medical Centers

brief_summary: This retrospective observational study investigated the correlation between foraminal imaging morphology (evaluated by MRI 4-level score and CT Haleem-Botchu classification) and the severity of clinical symptoms in patients with single-level degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis. A total of 120 adult patients treated between January 2024 and December 2025 were included. Patients were categorized into mild, moderate, and severe groups based on their Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores. The study analyzed the correlation of imaging grades with clinical functional scores (ODI and VAS) and identified independent imaging factors associated with symptom severity. No new treatments or extra hospital visits were involved.

title: Foraminal Imaging and Symptoms in Single-Level Degenerative Lumbar Stenosis

brief_summary:
Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is one of the most critical conditions in emergency medicine, causing high mortality and severe neurological sequelae due to the sudden cessation of circulation. Among the hundreds of thousands of patients affected worldwide, a significant proportion die or face permanent neurological impairment from hypoxic-ischemic brain injury, even after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Therefore, early and reliable assessment of brain injury after cardiac arrest is of great importance both for clinical decision-making and for the effective use of treatment resources.

Various methods are currently used to predict neurological prognosis after cardiac arrest, including computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, electroencephalography, and biochemical markers (NSE, S100B). However, some of these methods are expensive, have limited availability, or can be difficult to apply in the management of critically ill patients. In this context, bedside ultrasonography and cerebral oximetry, being applicable at the bedside, non-invasive, and repeatable, stand out as valuable alternative tools for clinicians.

Carotid Doppler ultrasonography provides indirect information about cerebral perfusion by measuring parameters such as peak systolic velocity (PSV), end-diastolic velocity (EDV), mean velocity (MV), pulsatility index (PI), and resistive index (RI) in the common carotid arteries. High PI and RI values indicate increased intracranial pressure or impaired cerebral vasomotor response, and these findings may be associated with poor neurological outcome. Similarly, transcranial Doppler (TCD) performed via the transtemporal approach reflects the integrity of cerebral autoregulation and cerebral perfusion pressure through middle cerebral artery (MCA) flow velocities and pulsatility values.

Optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) measurement is an increasingly widespread ultrasound application serving as a non-invasive indicator of elevated intracranial pressure. The optic nerve sheath is known to widen in the presence of cerebral edema, and this finding is thought to be associated with neurological deterioration.

Non-invasive cerebral oximetry (rSO2) continuously monitors frontal cerebral oxygen saturation, allowing early detection of periods of cerebral hypoxia. Inadequate cerebral oxygenation after cardiac arrest has been shown to be directly associated with poor prognosis. However, comprehensive studies interpreting this parameter together with Doppler ultrasonography findings are still lacking.

The primary aim of this study is to prospectively investigate the predictive value of carotid Doppler (internal, external, and common carotid arteries), TCD-MCA, and ONSD measurements, together with non-invasive cerebral oximetry values, for 60-day mortality and neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category, CPC scale) in patients admitted to the ICU due to OHCA. Secondary aims include examining the correlations between these parameters and determining the earliest and most reliable prognostic cut-off values.

The results of this study are expected to contribute to early neurological prognostication and patient management in ICU patients after OHCA
interventions: Carotid Doppler Ultrasonography, Transcranial Doppler, Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter Measurement, and Cerebral Oximetry
primary_outcomes: Association Between Carotid Doppler Indices and Neurological Outcome (CPC) After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
title: CAROTID DOPPLER AND CEREBRAL OXIMERY IN POST CARDIAC ARREST ICU PATIENTS

brief_summary:
Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is characterized by typical symptoms of heart failure, structural and functional cardiac abnormalities, and elevated serum levels of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. Typical symptoms of HFpEF include reduced exercise tolerance, exertional dyspnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and orthopnea.

It is estimated that approximately 35 million people worldwide suffer from HFpEF, including approximately 3 million patients in the United States. The exact number of patients with HFpEF remains unknown; however, the prevalence of the disease is increasing. Risk factors for HFpEF include obesity, arterial hypertension, atrial fibrillation, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and advanced age. Patients with HFpEF are hospitalized an average of 1.4 times per year, and the annual mortality rate is approximately 15%. To date, the most effective approach to the management of HFpEF has been the control of comorbidities, including diabetes mellitus, arterial hypertension, coronary artery disease, and obesity.

Remote rehabilitation (RR) has already become an established component of modern cardiology. It is widely used in developed countries, and its popularity continues to increase. Its main advantages include reduced costs for both patients and healthcare payers compared with traditional, center-based rehabilitation. In addition, for patients living far from rehabilitation centers or those with limited access to transportation, remote rehabilitation provides a solution to improve access to care.

The efficacy and safety of remote rehabilitation have been demonstrated in cardiac patients with coronary artery disease and in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). However, to date, the safety and efficacy of remote rehabilitation in patients with HFpEF have not been sufficiently investigated. Therefore, the aim of the proposed study is to assess the safety and efficacy of remote rehabilitation in patients with HFpEF.

brief_summary:
Endotracheal suctioning is a common procedure used to remove secretions from the airways of patients receiving mechanical ventilation. Although this procedure is necessary for respiratory care, it may cause pain and discomfort. Assessing pain can be challenging in patients who cannot communicate verbally, making appropriate pain assessment and management particularly important.

Natural sounds, such as sounds from nature, may offer a non-pharmacological approach to reducing procedural pain. Selecting sounds based on family members' knowledge of a patient's preferences may provide a more personalized approach, while standardized natural sounds may offer a consistent alternative. Noise reduction may also help limit unnecessary environmental sound exposure during the procedure.

This four-arm randomized controlled trial will compare the effects of family-proxy-selected natural sound therapy, standardized natural sound therapy, noise reduction, and the designated control condition on procedural pain during endotracheal suctioning in non-communicative adults receiving mechanical ventilation.

Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to one of the four study groups. Pain will be assessed using a prespecified instrument appropriate for non-communicative critically ill patients. The study will compare pain outcomes across the groups to determine whether family-proxy-selected natural sounds, standardized natural sounds, or noise reduction are associated with lower procedural pain.

The findings may help inform non-pharmacological approaches to procedural pain management in mechanically ventilated adults who cannot communicate their pain verbally.
interventions: Environmental Noise Reduction During Endotracheal Suctioning
primary_outcomes: Procedural Pain Score During Endotracheal Suctioning
title: Effects of Family-Proxy-Selected Natural Sound Therapy Versus Standardized Natural Sound and Noise Reduction on Procedural Pain During Endotracheal Suctioning in Non-Communicative Mechanically Ventilated Adults: A Four-Arm Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Chronic plantar heel pain is one of the most common musculoskeletal disorders affecting the foot and ankle region. It is frequently associated with plantar fasciitis and is characterized by pain at the medial calcaneal tubercle, especially during the first steps in the morning or after prolonged periods of rest. Chronic plantar heel pain negatively affects gait mechanics, balance, foot posture, functional activities. The condition is prevalent among physically active individuals, overweight adults, and people with prolonged standing occupations. Despite the availability of several conservative treatment approaches, optimal management remains controversial. Subtalar joint mobilization is commonly used in physiotherapy practice to improve joint biomechanics, restore mobility reduce pain, and enhance functional movement patterns. Similarly, foot core strengthening exercises aim to activate intrinsic foot muscles, improve medial longitudinal arch stability, and enhance dynamic balance and postural control. Recent evidence suggests that both interventions may independently improve symptoms associated with plantar heel pain; however, limited literature is available regarding their combined effectiveness.

The purpose of this study is to compare the effects of subtalar joint mobilization with and without foot core strengthening on pain, dynamic balance, foot posture and disability in patients with chronic plantar heel pain.

This study will be a randomized clinical trial conducted on individuals diagnosed with chronic plantar heel pain. Participants will be randomly allocated into two groups. Group A will receive subtalar joint mobilization +Baseline treatment, while Group B will receive subtalar joint mobilization combined with foot core strengthening exercises+baselinetreatment. Outcome measures will include Numeric Pain Scale (NPRS) for pain, Foot Function Index (FFI) for functional disability, Y-Balance Test or Star Excursion Balance Test for dynamic balance, Foot Posture Index-6 (FPI-6) for foot posture assessment.

The intervention protocol will be conducted over a specified treatment duration with pre- and post-treatment assessments. Data will be analysed using SPSS software. The findings of this study may provide evidence regarding a more effective rehabilitation strategy for patients with chronic plantar heel pain and may help physiotherapists improve clinical decision-making and patient outcomes.
interventions: Basline treatment+Subtalar joint mobilization +Foot core strengthening
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: NPRS
FOOT FUNCTION INDEX
FOOT POSTURE INDEX-6 (FPI-6)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether individualized oxygen adjustment during lung surgery lowers the risk of major complications. The study will include adults undergoing planned surgery on one lung that requires more than one hour of one-lung ventilation. One-lung ventilation means that only one lung is ventilated during part of the operation.

The main question is:

Does individualized oxygen adjustment, compared with continuous 100% oxygen, lower the risk of death or major complications within 30 days after surgery?

Researchers will enroll 628 participants at three hospitals in China. Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups:

* Individualized inspired oxygen titration group: The anesthesiologist will adjust the oxygen concentration according to blood oxygen saturation, measured continuously using a pulse oximeter.
* Pure oxygen group: The anesthesiologist will maintain 100% oxygen from the start of general anesthesia until removal of the tracheal tube.

Both groups will receive 100% oxygen before one-lung ventilation begins. In the individualized group, oxygen adjustment will continue after ventilation of both lungs resumes. Before removal of the tracheal tube, the anesthesiologist may raise the oxygen concentration for safety. Both groups will receive treatment if blood oxygen levels become too low.

Researchers will assess participants during hospitalization and through 30 days after surgery. Follow-up after discharge will take place by telephone or outpatient assessment. Researchers will compare deaths and major complications affecting the lungs, heart, brain, or kidneys. They will also assess recovery and safety.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants developing one or more major adverse events (MAEs)
title: Individualized Inspired Oxygen Fraction Titration During Lung Surgery (iOXY-LUNG)

This multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of different durations of neoadjuvant treatment with a PD-1 inhibitor, ipilimumab, and chemotherapy in patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). A total of 90 treatment-naïve patients with clinical stage IIA (primary tumor \>4 cm) to stage IIIB (limited to resectable N2 disease) NSCLC will be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to Cohort A (n=45) or Cohort B (n=45).

Patients in Cohort A will receive two cycles of a PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy and one cycle of ipilimumab, whereas patients in Cohort B will receive four cycles of a PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy and two cycles of ipilimumab. The PD-1 inhibitor will be administered intravenously at 200 mg every three weeks, and ipilimumab at 1 mg/kg every six weeks. Chemotherapy regimens will be selected according to histological subtype: pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for non-squamous NSCLC, and nab-paclitaxel plus carboplatin or cisplatin for squamous NSCLC.

Following neoadjuvant treatment, eligible patients will undergo curative-intent surgery within 22-42 days after the last treatment dose. Investigator-selected adjuvant therapy will begin 29-42 days after surgery. Tumor assessments will be performed according to RECIST version 1.1, with postoperative follow-up for up to five years.

The primary endpoint is the pathological complete response (pCR) rate, with treatment safety also being evaluated.
primary_outcomes: Pathological Complete Response (pCR) Rate
title: A Prospective Cohort Study of PD-1 Monoclonal Antibody Combined With Ipilimumab N01 and Chemotherapy in Perioperative Treatment of Resectable Non-small Cell Lung Cancer

This randomized controlled clinical trial aimed to evaluate the effects of a single preoperative intravenous dose of methylprednisolone on postoperative recovery following surgical extraction of impacted mandibular third molars (lower wisdom teeth).

The study included 30 patients who required surgical removal of impacted mandibular third molars on both sides. Using a split-mouth design, each patient underwent two separate surgical procedures, with an interval of at least four weeks between procedures. A total of 60 surgical extractions were performed.

Patients were allocated to three groups of 10 participants each. The study compared preoperative intravenous methylprednisolone (40 mg) with different medication protocols, including postoperative antibiotic treatment, preoperative antibiotic prophylaxis, and a control protocol.

The main outcomes included postoperative pain, facial swelling, and limitation of mouth opening (trismus). Blood markers of inflammation, including C-reactive protein (CRP), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), procalcitonin, and complete blood count parameters, were also evaluated. Clinical and laboratory measurements were obtained before surgery and during postoperative follow-up on days 1, 3, and 7.

The study sought to determine whether preoperative intravenous methylprednisolone was associated with differences in postoperative symptoms and inflammatory responses compared with the other medication protocols.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum C-Reactive Protein (CRP) Levels
Postoperative Pain Intensity (VAS Score)
title: Effects of Intravenous Methylprednisolone After Mandibular Third Molar Surgery

Heating the skin in this controlled way is intended to stimulate the body to produce new collagen, which may firm and smooth the skin over time.

Women aged 25 to 60 with mild to moderate facial skin laxity receive one treatment session to the face and neck at the first visit. They return for follow-up visits about 30 days and 90 days after treatment. At each visit, researchers take standardized 3D facial images, grade skin laxity and overall aesthetic improvement, and ask participants to complete questionnaires about how satisfied they are with their face and skin. Side effects such as redness, swelling, or discomfort are recorded throughout the study.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does one DENSITY treatment improve skin texture, pore appearance, and facial contour, as measured by 3D imaging?
* Do participants report greater satisfaction with their facial appearance and skin after treatment?
* Is the treatment safe and well tolerated?

brief_summary:
Artificial intelligence (AI), and particularly large language models (LLMs), is playing an increasingly important role in medical practice by facilitating documentation, data analysis, and communication with patients. These tools may improve access to medical information and reduce certain repetitive tasks; however, their use remains limited by risks of errors, hallucinations, variability in responses, and the lack of evaluation in real-world healthcare settings.

In the field of patient-provider communication, several studies have shown that AI-generated responses may be perceived as being as relevant as, or even more empathetic and clearer than, those provided by physicians. However, these findings are based predominantly on simulated scenarios and do not allow conclusions regarding the safety of autonomous use in clinical practice.

Managing patient inquiries outside scheduled consultations represents a substantial workload for healthcare teams. Generative AI could help address this demand, but its implementation requires medical oversight and rigorous safety evaluation.

The postoperative ENT setting provides a relevant area for investigation, as patients frequently experience symptoms that can be difficult to interpret, such as pain, bleeding, or wound-healing complications. A conversational agent could provide consistent responses and continuous accessibility; however, it should never replace on-call medical services. Its primary requirement is the ability to correctly identify situations requiring prompt or urgent medical assessment.

With this objective, a postoperative chatbot was developed using ChatGPT-4 through a secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture. Its knowledge base was restricted to recommendations from the French National Authority for Health (HAS), the French Society of Otorhinolaryngology (SFORL), and the PubMed literature in order to improve response reliability. An internal feasibility study yielded encouraging results: 68% of responses were rated as good to excellent by ENT experts, with writing quality and completeness sometimes exceeding those of practicing physicians, although clinicians remained superior in the nuanced assessment of clinical risk.

The objective of the present study is to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of this ENT postoperative follow-up chatbot among 100 ambulatory surgery patients treated at the Arthur Vernes Institute. The primary aim is to assess the patient experience before evaluating any potential impact on healthcare utilization or medico-economic outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Determine the effective use of the chatbot
title: Feasibility Study of a Conversational Chatbot for Outpatient Postoperative Follow-up in Otorhinolaryngology (ENT): Acceptability, Patterns of Use, and Patient Experience.

brief_summary: This prospective, single-center study at AIG Hospitals, Hyderabad, aims to establish normal 24-hour ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance values, including acid exposure time (AET), in 50 healthy Indian adults. Current Western diagnostic cut-offs may not be applicable to the Indian population, where normal AET is likely lower. Healthy volunteers aged 18-50 with no GI symptoms or systemic diseases will undergo baseline evaluations, high-resolution manometry, and 24-hour pH-impedance monitoring while maintaining regular activities. The study will assess how diet, body position, and sleep affect reflux, with statistical analysis to determine normative values for improved GERD diagnosis in India.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to investigate whether focused ultrasound of the chest can be used in a practical way in children with respiratory symptoms. The investigators will examine the different ways in which the ultrasound examination can be performed and what the examination may show in children with different types of respiratory symptoms.

The investigators will also investigate how this type of ultrasound examination can be introduced and used in everyday practice in a paediatric department. The results will help understand how chest ultrasound can best be used in children and which examination method is most suitable for future use.
primary_outcomes: Focused Thoracic ultrasound findings in a children admitted to a pediatric emergency department, divided into type
Characterization of findings on Focused Thoracic ultrasound, in a children admitted to a pediatric emergency department

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trail is to evaluate whether short-course telacebec-based regimens can induce rapid and measurable reductions in M. leprae viability, potentially establishing the foundation for future shorter, safer, and simplified therapeutic strategies for MB leprosy.

Participants will be randomised into one of the four study arms (A, B, C and D). The arm A is non interventional. For arms B, C, and D, the three-month study drug treatment will be followed by 9 months of MDT, bringing the total treatment time to 12 months. This provision of MDT ensures that the participant has received the recommended standard treatment for leprosy and is primarily for ethics considerations.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in viable Mycobacterium leprae load in participants' skin lesions
title: Telacebec in Adults With Multibacillary Leprosy (TEBULA Leprosy Trial)

brief_summary: This study is being done to compare three ways of using long-acting local pain medicine around the surgical wound during open lumbar fusion surgery. The goal is to learn which approach gives better pain relief after surgery, reduces the need for additional pain medicine such as tramadol, and causes fewer side effects such as nausea, vomiting, constipation, or wound problems. Participants will be adults aged 18 to under 75 years who are scheduled for open posterior lumbar fusion for degenerative lumbar disease and who agree to take part. They will be assigned to one of three local pain-relief regimens: liposomal bupivacaine, a standard local anesthetic cocktail, or a modified cocktail that adds magnesium sulfate. Pain scores, rescue pain medicine, side effects, quality-of-life scores, and recovery information such as length of hospital stay will be recorded during the hospital stay and up to 72 hours after surgery. This study compares marketed local anesthetics and commonly used additives in routine surgical care; it is not a first-in-human or new-drug study. The results may help doctors choose a safer and more effective pain-control plan after lumbar fusion
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital of Kunming Medical University
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity Assessed by VAS Within 72 Hours After Surgery
Total Rescue Tramadol Consumption Within 72 Hours After Surgery
Incidence of Adverse Events Within 72 Hours After Surgery
title: Comparing Long-Acting Local Pain Relief Methods in PLIF Surgery

brief_summary:
MK-7602 is a new medicine that is being studied to treat malaria. Malaria is a disease caused by a parasite that spreads to people through mosquito bites. Symptoms of malaria include fever, chills, and flu-like illness. If malaria is not treated, some people can have serious problems that can be deadly.

The goal of this trial is to learn what happens to MK-7602 in a person's body over time (a pharmacokinetic or PK trial). Researchers will compare what happens to MK-7602 in people's blood when it is taken alone (Period 1) and in combination with another medicine called pyronaridine (Period 2). Researchers also want to learn about the safety of MK-7602 taken with and without pyronaridine and if people tolerate them.

brief_summary:
This study is designed as a prospective, post-market, multi-center, single-arm study to collect real-world data of the VCFix Spinal System used in US clinical practice.

Approximately 5 centers in the US will enroll subjects with VCF in a non-randomized fashion, and VCFix will be used within its cleared purpose and indications for use.

The study has been designed to be methodologically compatible with the EU EXPAND (CIP-VS02-EU) study, thereby aiming for the pooling of data to the EU study. Data pooling will be pursued only as a sensitivity analysis if pre-specified similarity criteria are met. The US study provides meaningful real-world evidence regardless of pooling feasibility.

The targeted patient population, assessment schedule, and study endpoints are therefore similar to those of the EU EXPAND study.
interventions: VCFix Spinal System in stand-alone configuration

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate the diagnostic utility of whole-body ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT in adults with cavernous sinus syndrome (CSS) in whom magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) failed to establish the underlying cause. The study also compares the performance of ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT with paired ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can whole-body ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT detect and characterize cavernous sinus lesions and disease extent in patients with MRI-indeterminate CSS? Does ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT provide superior lesion conspicuity and help identify safer biopsy sites compared with ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT? Researchers will compare whole-body ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT with paired ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT to evaluate lesion detection, quantitative imaging parameters, disease extent, and their impact on identifying appropriate biopsy targets.
lead_sponsor: Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic performance of ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT for detection of cavernous sinus lesions compared with paired ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT
title: Whole-Body ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT in Cavernous Sinus Syndrome: A Prospective Comparison With ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to test whether screening all major blunt trauma patients for blood vessel injuries in the neck and head using CT scans (universal screening) leads to fewer strokes and stroke-related deaths compared to screening only selected patients who meet specific risk criteria (selective screening).

This is a pilot feasibility study. The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Can trauma centers that currently use selective screening successfully switch to universal screening? Are the definitions used to identify and measure outcomes clear and applied consistent across all participating hospitals? Do stroke complications occur frequently enough to support a larger, future clinical trial? Can participating trauma centers reliably track and report the number of CT scans performed for this purpose?

Participating trauma centers in the study will: Continue using their existing selective screening approach at the start of the study Switch to universal CT screening of all major blunt trauma patients at an assigned point during the 12-month study period Submit de-identified patient data to the coordinating center using a secure electronic database Researchers will use the result of this initial feasibility study to determine whether a larger clinical trial comparing the two screening strategies is feasible.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants with BCVI-related Ischemic Stroke
title: Universal Screening for Blunt Cerebrovascular Injury

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial will evaluate the effectiveness of a web-based sustainable food literacy program for university students in Taiwan.

A total of 180 university students will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: a sustainable food literacy intervention group, a general nutrition education comparison group, or a control group. The two educational programs will be delivered online over 6 weeks and will include 11 learning units.

Participants in all three groups will complete assessments before the intervention, immediately after the 6-week intervention period, and 3 months after the intervention. The primary outcome is comprehensive food literacy. Other outcomes include different domains of food literacy, sustainable eating intentions and strategies, and healthy eating behaviors.

The study aims to determine whether the sustainable food literacy program improves food literacy compared with the control condition and whether it provides additional benefits compared with general nutrition education.
lead_sponsor: Kaohsiung Medical University Chung-Ho Memorial Hospital
primary_outcomes: Comprehensive Food Literacy Total Score
title: Web-Based Sustainable Food Literacy Program for University Students

brief_summary:
Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is the leading cause of infectious diarrhea among older adults. The epidemiology of community-acquired CDI, particularly among residents of long-term care facilities, remains poorly understood to this day. While numerous studies on the epidemiology, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of CDI have been conducted in hospital settings, primary care often lags behind these advances. Limited access to diagnostic tests and treatment options, as well as insufficient resources allocated to preventing cross-transmission, are all factors that hinder the control of ICD in long-term care facilities. This will be the first French study on the epidemiology of ICD among nursing home residents, which can serve as a reference for implementing a multidisciplinary action plan and measuring its impact. This will be carried out as part of a city-hospital collaboration and will facilitate the creation of a healthcare network involving multiple healthcare providers, such as general practitioners working in nursing homes, clinical laboratories, pharmacies, dietitians and nutritionists, and the university hospital.

A better understanding of the epidemiology of ICD among residents in long-term care facilities and an assessment of professional practices related to ICD risk prevention should enable us to better target strategies for improving care while raising awareness among healthcare providers and public health policymakers. We therefore plan to optimize the impact of implementing a multidisciplinary action program aligned with the expectations of frontline practitioners regarding the reduction of the risk of ICD (training, prevention tools, diagnosis and treatment of ICD, appropriate use of antibiotics, nutritional counseling, prescribing probiotics, and establishing a coordinated care pathway for ICD). The implementation of this action program is expected to reduce the incidence rate of ICD, the recurrence rate, and antibiotic use in nursing homes, as well as the number of transfers to the hospital for ICD management.
primary_outcomes: Incidence Rate of ICD
title: Epidemiology of Clostridioides Difficile Infection (CDI) in Long-term Care Facilities, Assessment of Professional Practices Related to CDI Risk Prevention, and Strategies for Improving Care.

brief_summary:
T2D is a chronic disease that forces people with diabetes to take their medications as prescribed and adhere to the recommended self-care practices to control their blood sugar and prevent complications. For a few patients, however, poor medication adherence is a problem due to forgetfulness, medication concerns, side effects, scheduling of medications in daily life, lack of access to medication, or lack of social support.

Researchers want to see whether a customized nurse-led counseling service is effective in enhancing adherence to diabetes medications for adults with type 2 diabetes in a randomized controlled trial. The study will also explore the impact of the intervention on glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels when compared to usual care.

Participants who meet the criteria will be randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a usual care control group. Intervention group will be given a structured nurse-led counseling program, tailored to them, for 5 consecutive days. Assessment of medication taking barriers, providing education on medication adherence, problem solving strategies, individual goal setting, and development of a personal action plan will be incorporated into the program. A primary identified barrier to medication adherence will be identified and used to guide the counseling provided.

The participants in the control group will be provided with standard diabetes care, as provided by the study site's services. Prespecified outcomes will be measured at baseline and at follow-up, including adherence to medication. HbA1c will be determined per study protocol to assess glycemic control.

The results could guide the potential for a brief, individualized nurse-led counselling program as a feasible intervention for promoting adherence to treatment and self-management of diabetes in adults with type 2 diabetes.
primary_outcomes: Change in Medication Adherence Score from Baseline to Follow-Up
title: A Nurse-Led Personalized Self-Management Counseling Intervention to Improve Medication Adherence and Glycemic Control in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
ROCKET evaluates the clinical performance of an investigational version of neos™, a non-invasive device that uses a virtual-reality headset and eye tracking to assess binocular vision-how the two eyes work together.

The study compares neos™ results with standard clinical examinations for three functions: sensory fusion, the ability to combine images from both eyes into a single image; stereopsis, the perception of depth from differences between the images seen by each eye; and suppression, reduced awareness of visual input from one eye during binocular viewing.

Approximately 184 patients aged 3 years and older who require a clinical binocular vision assessment will participate at ophthalmology centres in Switzerland. Each participant will undergo standard clinical testing and a neos™ examination during a single study visit. During the neos™ examination, visual stimuli are presented through the headset while the device records eye movements and pupil responses.

The main objective is to determine how accurately neos™ identifies the presence or absence of sensory fusion, stereopsis and central suppression compared with the clinical reference assessments. Additional analyses will compare fusion-related measurements, characterize stereopsis and suppression, and explore relationships between neos™ measurements and clinical findings.
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity and Specificity of neos™ for Detecting Sensory Fusion
Sensitivity and Specificity of neos™ for Detecting Stereopsis
Sensitivity and Specificity of neos™ for Detecting Central Suppression
title: Assessment of Binocular Vision Function With Neos™ (ROCKET)

brief_summary:
This single-center, randomized controlled trial with parallel groups, consists of an intensive nutritional intervention based on a high-fiber Mediterranean diet (target intake: 30-35 g/day of dietary fiber), which will be compared with a control group receiving low-intensity nutritional counseling on the Mediterranean diet. The intervention will last 16 weeks, followed by an 8-month follow-up period to evaluate its impact and the sustainability of long-term effects.

Participants allocated to the intervention group will receive nutritional counseling and guidance to achieve the intervention target of a daily dietary fiber intake of 30 to 35 g. To this end, they will be provided with a personalized weekly meal plan and will undergo intensive follow-up throughout the intervention period.

Participants in the control group will receive educational materials on how to follow a Mediterranean diet; however, no specific dietary fiber intake targets will be established, and they will not receive a personalized weekly meal plan.

brief_summary: This pilot study will examine whether a single dental implant can be placed safely without giving antibiotics before or after surgery in patients with straightforward cases in Vietnam. Adults who are generally healthy, have one missing back tooth, and have enough bone for an implant will have the implant placed with standard infection-control measures (antiseptic mouth rinse, a surgical guide, and ibuprofen for relieving the pain) but no preventive antibiotics. Antibiotics will be given only if an infection develops. Participants will be seen 2 days, 7 days, 14 days, 1 month and 3 months after surgery. The main outcome is early implant failure, meaning the implant is lost before the replacement tooth is fitted. We will also record infection, pain, painkiller use, and gum health around the implant. The study will enroll 39 participants at the dental specialty clinic of the University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City.

brief_summary:
This study tests whether adding CHW support to usual nutrition care helps adults with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, or chronic kidney disease manage their diet and health. At Caridad Center, a free clinic in Palm Beach County, Florida, usual care includes medical nutrition therapy from a registered dietitian and medically tailored groceries. Many patients find it hard to keep up dietary changes because of limited nutrition knowledge, cooking skills, food costs, and cultural fit.

Two hundred adults will be randomly assigned to usual care or usual care plus INTEGRATE-CHW, a 12-week program of six sessions with a trained CHW. In each session the participant selects one or two goals from the dietitian's plan and builds an action plan with the CHW. The dietitian remains responsible for the nutrition plan. The study will compare nutrition self-efficacy, nutrition literacy, diet quality, food security, and clinical measures between groups at baseline and Week 12. It will also evaluate how well the program fits into routine clinic care.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if proton moderately hypofractionated radiotherapy works to treat non-small cell lung cancer in adults who cannot tolerate standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy. It will also learn about the safety of this treatment. The main questions it aims to answer are: Does proton moderately hypofractionated radiotherapy improve the 1-year overall survival rate compared with historical data from similar patients? What medical problems do participants have during and after this treatment? This is a single-arm study, so all participants will receive proton radiotherapy. Researchers will compare results with historical control data, not with a placebo group. Participants will: Receive proton radiotherapy once daily for about 3 to 4 weeks.

Have checkups and tests before treatment, weekly during treatment, and regularly after treatment. Complete follow-up visits for at least 2 years, including imaging, blood tests, lung function tests, and quality-of-life questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: 1-Year Overall Survival (OS) Rate
