brief_summary:
BACKGROUND. Portal hypertension-related gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB), especially gastric variceal bleeding, is a critical complication of liver cirrhosis that is associated with high rebleeding and mortality rates. While endovascular interventions such as transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) and retrograde/antegrade transvenous obliteration (RTO/ATO) represent major advances, real-world clinical data and localized prognostic models for patients undergoing these treatments are extremely sparse in Vietnam.

OBJECTIVE. This study aims to describe the clinical and laboratory characteristics, evaluate technical and clinical treatment outcomes, and identify independent pre-procedural prognostic factors associated with adverse clinical outcomes after endovascular interventions.

METHODS. A hybrid cohort study combining a retrospective phase (January 2021 - September 2026, target n=117) and a prospective phase (October 2026 - March 2028, target n=50) will be conducted at the University Medical Center Ho Chi Minh City. The total sample size of 167 patients is powered using Cochran's single proportion formula and the rule of 10 events per variable (EPV) for logistic regression modeling. Demographics, lab markers, hepatic scoring systems (Child-Pugh, MELD, MELD-Na, MELD 3.0,...), procedural parameters, and clinical outcomes (initial bleeding control, rebleeding, in-hospital and 6-week mortality) will be recorded. Univariate and multivariate logistic and Cox proportional hazard regression will be used to analyze predictors of outcomes.

IMPACT. The TOPIC study will establish the first systematic real-world clinical database of endovascular portal hypertension interventions in Vietnam. Defining localized prognostic variables will support risk stratification, optimize patient selection, lower healthcare costs, and establish practical guidelines for personalized clinical management.
interventions: Endovascular Intervention for Portal Hypertension-Related Gastrointestinal Bleeding
lead_sponsor: University Medical Center Ho Chi Minh City (UMC)
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With a Composite Adverse Clinical Outcome After Endovascular Intervention
title: Treatment Outcomes and Predictors After Endovascular Intervention for Portal Hypertension-Related Gastrointestinal Bleeding in Cirrhosis

brief_summary:
Some people feel worried about being awake during hand surgery. In a method called wide-awake local anesthesia no tourniquet (WALANT), the hand is numbed with local anesthetic, and surgery is performed without a tourniquet. This study examined whether extra information and comfort measures could reduce anxiety shortly after surgery compared with usual care.

The study included 120 adults undergoing non-emergency hand surgery at one hospital in Türkiye. Patients were randomly assigned to two groups, with 60 people in each group. Both groups received WALANT surgery.

One group watched a short educational video before surgery, received structured explanations from the surgeon, was asked to take a deep breath as the local anesthetic needle was inserted, and listened to music of their choice during surgery. The other group received usual care, including standard explanations about the surgery and anesthesia.

Patients completed an anxiety questionnaire before the additional measures and again 10 to 30 minutes after surgery. Researchers also assessed pain during local anesthetic injection, patient satisfaction after surgery, and whether patients would choose or recommend WALANT in the future.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative State Anxiety Score Measured by the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI-I)
title: Effects of an Anxiety-Reduction Program in Adults Undergoing Awake Hand Surgery

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to learn whether weighted blankets help reduce agitation, such as restlessness or excessive movement, in adults in an intensive care unit (ICU). Researchers will compare a weighted blanket with a standard blanket and usual comfort measures. They will also examine safety and the use of medicines given as needed to manage agitation or anxiety.

After a three-patient pilot to test study procedures, 197 adults will be assigned by chance to one of two groups. One group will receive a weighted blanket, and the other will receive a standard blanket with usual comfort measures. Both groups will receive similar nursing attention and continue all needed medical care. Weighted blanket sessions may last 15 minutes to 2 hours, up to twice daily, with close monitoring.

Researchers will compare agitation before and after each session, with the main comparison at 1 hour. They will also examine vital signs, medicine use, safety events, time in the ICU, and days requiring a breathing machine. Participation may or may not improve comfort or agitation.
interventions: Attention Control: Standard Blanket and Usual Comfort Measures
primary_outcomes: Change in Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) Score
title: Weighted Blankets for Agitation in Adults in the Intensive Care Unit

brief_summary: Brief SummaryCopy and paste the text below into the Brief Summary text box:The purpose of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to evaluate and compare the clinical, radiographic, and histological outcomes of horizontal ridge augmentation in single edentulous sites in the esthetic zone using a Leukocyte- and Platelet-Rich Fibrin (L-PRF) Block versus a composite graft of autogenous bone and deproteinized bovine bone mineral (DBBM). Following tooth loss, the alveolar ridge undergoes physiological bone resorption, particularly at the thin facial bone wall in the anterior maxilla. Adequate bone volume is required to allow dental implant placement in an ideal prosthetically driven position and to support long-term peri-implant soft tissue stability. Guided bone regeneration (GBR) using a 1:1 composite graft of autogenous bone and DBBM covered by a collagen membrane is considered an established standard technique. However, harvesting autogenous bone requires a secondary surgical donor site, which increases surgical time, patient discomfort, and surgical morbidity. The L-PRF Block combines DBBM particles with patient-derived blood concentrates rich in fibrin and growth factors, eliminating the need for autogenous bone harvesting. In this single-blind, non-inferiority clinical trial, 70 adult patients requiring horizontal ridge augmentation in the esthetic zone before implant placement will be randomly assigned (1:1 ratio) to receive either:Test Group: Horizontal ridge augmentation using an L-PRF Block (DBBM + L-PRF membranes + liquid fibrinogen) covered with a resorbable collagen membrane. Control Group: Horizontal ridge augmentation using a composite graft (1:1 ratio of autogenous bone harvested from the mandibular symphysis and DBBM) covered with a resorbable collagen membrane. Patients will undergo 3D Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) imaging before surgery ($T\_0$), immediately postoperatively ($T\_1$), and 6 months post-augmentation ($T\_2$). At 6 months ($T\_2$), bone core biopsies will be harvested during implant placement for histological and histomorphometric analysis. Primary implant stability (ISQ) will be recorded at implant placement ($T\_2$), and secondary implant stability (ISQ) will be measured at abutment connection ($T\_3$). Patient-reported outcomes (pain and satisfaction with esthetics/function) and buccal bone plate thickness will be evaluated 6 months after final prosthetic restoration ($T\_4$). The trial aims to test whether the L-PRF Block is non-inferior to the conventional autogenous/DBBM composite graft.
primary_outcomes: Horizontal Bone Gain
title: L-PRF Block vs Composite Graft for Horizontal Ridge Augmentation

brief_summary:
The aim of this clinical trial is to investigate the effects of a six-week targeted affective cognitive training, combining virtual reality and computer-based exercises, in symptomatically stable patients with mood disorders (major depressive disorder or bipolar disorder) and unaffected first-degree relatives.

The investigators hypothesize that targeted affective cognitive training, compared with treatment as usual, will improve affective cognition (primary outcome), assessed using a composite measure of emotion regulation and facial emotion recognition.

Secondly, the investigators hypothesize that the training will improve self-reported emotion regulation abilities and associated neural activity during emotion regulation, including changes in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex activity.

Finally, the investigators will explore whether the training affects broader cognitive functioning, psychosocial functioning, quality of life, and longer-term clinical outcomes, including relapse or onset of mood disorder.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a six-month exercise program that combines rowing, walking, and adapted physical activity (such as yoga or Pilates) can improve health and quality of life in women aged 40 to 65 who have had surgery for breast cancer and have completed their post-surgery treatments. Regular exercise is known to benefit cancer survivors, but many women become much less active during and after treatment and do not return to their previous levels. Group water sports such as dragon boat paddling have shown promising results, while very few studies have looked at rowing. This study will also learn about the safety of the program and about how the body responds to rowing.

The main questions it aims to answer are whether the program improves physical fitness, including aerobic capacity, hand grip strength, flexibility, and body composition, and whether it improves quality of life and reduces cancer-related fatigue. The study also asks whether practicing rowing brings psychological benefits, such as higher self-esteem, greater enjoyment of physical activity, and a better sense of satisfaction in three areas of life: work, friendship, and love. In addition, it will examine what energy and oxygen demands rowing places on the body, and whether the program is safe and feasible, by recording any exercise-related adverse events and how many of the scheduled sessions participants complete.

Before joining, participants will be recruited through the hospital's Breast Unit and will need medical clearance from a physiatrist and a sports medicine physician, who will check their health and eligibility. Participants will then follow the six-month program, doing every week one hour of rowing at a rowing club, one hour of walking on their own, and one hour of adapted physical activity, yoga, or Pilates delivered online by qualified instructors. Rowing sessions will take place in stable boats designed for beginners, in small groups of no more than ten women, with certified instructors, a psychologist, and trained volunteers supervising from the water. Exercises will be adapted to each woman's starting level and will progress gradually. At the start, after three months, and at the end of the program, participants will complete fitness tests (a submaximal cycling test, hand grip strength, flexibility, and body measurements) and questionnaires on physical activity, quality of life, fatigue, self-esteem, enjoyment of exercise, and life satisfaction. After each training session they will also rate how hard it felt, and during selected rowing training sessions, a portable face-worn device will measure their breathing and oxygen use while they are rowing.
primary_outcomes: Change in estimated maximal aerobic capacity (VO2max)
Change in health-related quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30)
Change in self-esteem (Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale)
Change in enjoyment of physical activity (PACES)
Metabolic responses to rowing (oxygen uptake and heart rate)
title: Rowing-Based Exercise Intervention on Health and Quality of Life in Breast Cancer Survivors

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial compared closure versus non-closure of the fascia at the working port (trocar) sites during laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy for severe obesity.

A total of 160 adult patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy at Kasr Al Ainy Hospital, Cairo University, were randomly allocated (1:1) to non-closure of the working ports (skin closure only) or fascial closure of the working ports using a fascial closure device.

Patients were followed for one year for the development of port-site hernia. Postoperative pain was assessed with the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) at one week and one month, and functional recovery with the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at one week.
interventions: Non-closure of working port fascia (skin closure only)
primary_outcomes: Incidence of port-site hernia
title: Closure Versus Non-Closure of Working Ports in Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to optimize treatment strategies for Chinese patients with treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS). It will compare two types of treatment:

1. Drug therapy with clozapine alone or in combination with other medications.
2. Neuromodulation therapy, modified electroconvulsive therapy (MECT) or magnetic seizure therapy (MST).

The study aims to determine which approach provides better symptom improvement, fewer cognitive side effects, and greater overall safety. The results may provide important clinical evidence to guide future treatment decisions for patients with TRS.
primary_outcomes: PANSS reduction rate at Week 8 during the pharmacological optimization phase
PANSS reduction rate at Week 4 during the neuromodulation phase
title: Sequential Treatment Approaches for Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to test whether adding a collagen protein scaffold can improve cartilage repair of talus injury, compared to standard surgery alone. The study will enroll 40 patients (aged 18-55) with talus cartilage damage who haven't responded to conservative treatments.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the collagen scaffold help regenerate better-quality cartilage (measured by MRI scans at 3/6 months and 1/2 years)?
* Do patients experience better pain relief and ankle function after this combined treatment?

Researchers will compare two groups:

* Experimental group: Receives microfracture surgery + collagen scaffold implant
* Active Comparator group: Receives microfracture surgery alone

Participants will:

* Undergo arthroscopic surgery (either procedure)
* Complete follow-up visits at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year and 2 years
* Have MRI scans and functional assessments
* Report pain levels and daily activity limitations through questionnaires
primary_outcomes: MOCART score
title: A RCT of Collagen Scaffold for the Repair of Talus Cartilage Injury

brief_summary: This multicenter, randomized, open-label, noninferiority trial will compare two high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) target-guided colchicine strategies in 1,768 adults with very-high-risk coronary artery disease after percutaneous coronary intervention, LDL cholesterol ≤1.4 mmol/L, and residual inflammation (hs-CRP 2.0-10.0 mg/L). Participants will be assigned 1:1 to a standard target of 1.0 to \<2.0 mg/L or an intensive target of \<1.0 mg/L. Both groups will start colchicine 0.25 mg orally once daily, with dose adjustments guided by hs-CRP and tolerability. The primary outcome is the 18-month composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal ischemic stroke, or ischemia-driven revascularization. The noninferiority hypothesis compares the standard target strategy with the intensive target strategy, with a prespecified hazard-ratio margin of 1.30.
primary_outcomes: Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events Through 18 Months
title: Hs-CRP-Guided Colchicine Treatment Targets in Very-High-Risk Patients With Coronary Artery Disease After PCI (TARGET-CHD)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to find out whether phenotype-based pain management guidelines can effectively and safely reduce head and neck cancer-related pain in adults with head and neck cancer who have not yet started cancer treatment.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do phenotype-based pain management guidelines reduce pain in people with head and neck cancer within the first week of treatment?
* Are the guidelines safe, based on the number and type of medication-related side effects experienced by participants?

Participants will:

* Attend three study visits over approximately one week (at baseline, after 3 days, and after 7 days or before starting cancer treatment, whichever comes first).
* Complete questionnaires about their pain, anxiety, depression, medication side effects, and use of breakthrough pain medication.
* Undergo a detailed examination to identify the type (phenotype) of their pain.
* Receive a treatment plan tailored to their pain phenotype, which may include pain-relieving medications, muscle relaxants, medicines for nerve pain or burning pain, and opioid medications when needed based on pain severity.
* Return for follow-up visits to assess changes in pain, medication side effects, and use of breakthrough pain medication.
lead_sponsor: Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital & Research Centre
primary_outcomes: Pain relief
title: Effectiveness of Phenotype-based Pain Management Guidelines for Head and Neck Cancer Related Pain: a Pilot Study

brief_summary: To learn if the combination of golcadomide, obinutuzumab, glofitamab, and polatuzumab vedotin in LBCL participants can help to control the disease.
primary_outcomes: Safety and adverse events (AEs)
title: Smart 3: A Multi-Center Phase 2 Trial Of Golcadomide, Glofitamab And Polatuzumab Vedotin (G2P) For Patients With Newly Diagnosed Large B-Cell Lymphoma

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effects of short-term environmental comfort interventions and oral motor stimulation on comfort and oral feeding readiness in preterm infants. A total of 84 preterm infants who are clinically stable and transitioning to oral feeding will be assigned to one of four groups: massage, white noise, oral stimulation, or routine care (control). Before the intervention, infant comfort and oral feeding readiness will be assessed using the Premature Infant Comfort Scale and the Preterm Oral Feeding Readiness Assessment Scale (POFRAS). Infants in the intervention groups will receive a single 5-minute session of massage, white noise, or oral stimulation before their first oral feeding, while infants in the control group will receive routine care. Comfort and oral feeding readiness will be assessed during the study to compare the effects of the interventions. The study will also examine the relationship between comfort and oral feeding readiness in preterm infants.
primary_outcomes: Change in Premature Infant Comfort Scale Score
Change in Preterm Oral Feeding Readiness Assessment Scale Score
title: Effects of Environmental Comfort and Oral Motor Stimulation on Comfort and Oral Feeding Readiness in Preterm Infants

brief_summary: The goal of this observational study is to learn about the efficacy-safety profiles of combined hepatic arterial embolization (TAE) and laparoscopic radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in patients with hepatic hemangioma who receive sequential TAE-RFA treatment. The main question it aims to answer is: Does the time interval between TAE and subsequent RFA influence therapeutic efficacy and safety in patients with hepatic hemangioma receiving sequential TAE-RFA therapy? Participants already undergoing TAE followed by RFA as part of their regular clinical management for hepatic hemangioma will undergo scheduled laboratory tests and contrast-enhanced abdominal CT examinations over a 12-month follow-up period.
primary_outcomes: Tumour volume reduction rate
title: Observation Study on the Efficacy and Safety of Hepatic Artery Embolization Combined With Radiofrequency Ablation for Hepatic Hemangioma: The Impact of Different Treatment Intervals

brief_summary: To assess the value of deep NGS-MRD detection for risk stratification in adult high-risk acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, in this prospective, single-center, observational cohort study following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). A total of 169 patients will be enrolled, and deep NGS-MRD testing will be performed at approximately +3 months after transplantation. Patients will be stratified into NGS-MRD-positive and NGS-MRD-negative groups based on test results. No investigational interventions will be administered. Follow-up analyses will evaluate the associations between NGS-MRD status and post-transplant relapse and survival.
lead_sponsor: Institute of Hematology & Blood Diseases Hospital, China
primary_outcomes: 6-month cumulative incidence of relapse
title: Risk Stratification Value of Deep NGS-MRD Detection in Acute Myeloid Leukemia Patients After Allo-HSCT

brief_summary: This randomized clinical trial will compare plyometric and calisthenic training in 44 karate athletes at Hayatabad Sports Complex, Peshawar, split into two groups of 22 and trained three times a week for 6 weeks. Jump performance will be measured with the wall-based vertical jump test and knee function with the Kujala Anterior Knee Pain Scale, to see which method better improves jump performance

Wall-based vertical jump method:
title: PLYOMETRIC TRAINING VERSUS CALISTHENIC TECHNIQUE FOR IMPROVING JUMP PERFORMANCE AND PATELLOFEMORAL FUNCTION IN KARATE ATHLETES

brief_summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia worldwide and involves systemic alterations beyond the brain, such as loss of muscle strength, chronic low-grade inflammation, and gut microbiome dysbiosis. Physical exercise is a promising non-pharmacological therapy, and velocity-based resistance training has proven safe and effective in older adults. However, the effects of performing resistance exercises at high versus moderate velocity in people with AD remain unknown, and human evidence on how exercise modulates the gut microbiome in AD is very limited. This study aims to assess and compare the effects of two velocity-based resistance training modalities (high load at moderate velocity and moderate load at high velocity) versus usual care on the gut microbiome, systemic inflammation, plasma biomarkers, biological age, and intrinsic capacity in older adults with mild-to-moderate AD, using cognitively healthy older adults as a reference group.

Biological age
title: Exercise in Alzheimer's Disease: Functional Biomarkers

brief_summary:
The main purpose of this study is to measure the amount of imlunestrant that gets into the bloodstream and how long it takes the body to get rid of it when given in two different formulations. This study also compares the two different formulations of imlunestrant against the effects of food and omeprazole in the body.

For each participant, the study may last up to 2.5 months and participants can expect to stay in the clinical research unit (CRU) up to 27 days over several visits.
primary_outcomes: Pharmacokinetics (PK): Maximum Concentration (Cmax) of Imlunestrant (Freebase)
2. PK: Area Under the Concentration Versus Time Curve (AUC) of Imlunestrant (Freebase)
title: A Study of Imlunestrant (LY3484356) in Healthy Female Participants

brief_summary:
The study will evaluate the safety and preliminary efficacy of saxagliptin in treating prolonged DoC through a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, delayed start Phase IIA trial. Twenty-four (24) patients with prolonged DOC (≥28 days post-injury) will be enrolled at Rehabilitation Hopsital's Center for Disorders of Consciousness (C³DoC).

Twelve patients will be randomized to receive placebo for 15 days followed by saxagliptin 5 mg for 15 days (Delayed Start Group), and 12 will receive saxagliptin 5 mg for the full 30 days (Full Treatment Group). Patients will be under continuous medical monitoring within C³DoC throughout their approximately 4-week admission. Validated behavioral biomarkers of consciousness (CRS-R) will be collected by blinded certified assessors at baseline (days -7 and 0), day 15, and day 30, with portable EEG-based AI biomarker assessments to corroborate behavioral findings. Follow-up DRS-PI assessments will be conducted at days 60 and 90.

A pre-planned adaptive dose escalation design will be employed. The first 6 patients (sentinel cohort) will receive 5 mg (or placebo per delayed start). Upon cohort completion, the independent Safety Monitoring Board (SMB), chaired by a Medical doctor , will review unblinded safety data. If IRB and FDA IND Exemption approval is obtained for dose escalation, and excellent safety criteria are met (zero SAEs, no Grade 2+ AEs, zero hypoglycemia), the SMB will direct escalation to 10 mg for subsequent patients (up to 400 mg/day has been shown to be well-tolerated in humans); otherwise, 5 mg continues. Investigators and patients remain blinded throughout.
lead_sponsor: Casa Colina Hospital and Centers for Healthcare
primary_outcomes: Incidence of serious adverse events (SAEs)
Change in CRS-R total score from baseline to Day 15 (placebo-controlled comparison) and Day 30.
title: Restoring Awareness

brief_summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) has shifted toward a patient-personalized precision medicine paradigm; however, the high heterogeneity and complex tumor microenvironment (TME) of CRC restrict the development of individualized therapy, and existing preclinical models and multi-omics technologies are insufficient to broadly benefit patients. Building on previous research, this project intends to use 3D multicellular bioprinting (3DMP) to incorporate key TME components-cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and PBMC immune cells-to construct patient-derived CRC-CAFs/PBMC 3DMP models, aiming to apply them to personalized clinical drug screening and prognosis prediction, and to combine them with multi-omics technologies to advance preclinical research on CRC. The implementation of this study will help address the bottleneck of the lack of broadly applicable preclinical models for advancing CRC precision therapy. It has major clinical translational value, will bring significant changes to CRC preclinical research platforms, and will help promote the development of cancer precision medicine.
primary_outcomes: Response of 3D tumor models/organoids to the same chemotherapy drugs as the corresponding patients.
title: A Patient-Derived 3D Bioprinted Colorectal Cancer-Stroma-Immune Triad Model Uncovers Microenvironmental Mechanisms of Chemoresistance and Immune Evasion

brief_summary:
The CLEAN ACNE Study is a prospective, observational, Phase IV, open-label, multicenter, single-arm study at 3-5 sites in Vietnam. It will describe the safety, tolerability, and clinical effectiveness of adapalene 0.1%/clindamycin 1% fixed-dose combination gel (Klenzit®-C) as used in routine clinical practice. Participants are Vietnamese patients aged 12 years and older with mild to moderate acne vulgaris.

Patients whose treating physician has already prescribed Klenzit®-C as part of routine care will be invited to take part. The decision to prescribe is made independently of the study. About 360 participants will apply the gel once daily, preferably in the evening, for 12 weeks. Study visits take place at baseline and at Weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12.

The main focus is safety and tolerability. This includes adverse events and local skin reactions such as redness, dryness, darkening of the skin, peeling, and itching. The study will also observe changes in inflammatory and non-inflammatory acne lesion counts. It will record the proportion of participants who reach treatment success on the Investigator Global Assessment (IGA) at Weeks 4, 8, and 12. An interim safety review will take place at Week 2, once about half of the participants have enrolled.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Adverse Events (AEs), Serious Adverse Events (SAEs), Treatment-Related AEs and SAEs, and AEs Leading to Discontinuation
title: Safety, Tolerability, and Clinical Effectiveness of Adapalene/Clindamycin Phosphate Gel (Klenzit®-C) in Vietnamese Patients With Mild to Moderate Acne Vulgaris

brief_summary: ComPARE is a cross-sectional observational study investigating the effectiveness of communication during prenatal consultations concerning vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC). It involves 50 pregnant people considering VBAC and 12 healthcare professionals from IRCCS Ospedale San Raffaele: 6 OB-GYNs and 6 midwives with expertise in VBAC. The main objective is to identify and analyse misunderstandings in doctor/midwife-patient communication, using the TouCAN Codebook, and to examine whether these misunderstandings are associated with patients' perceptions of communication quality. The study does not introduce any treatment or medical device: it analyses routine clinical consultations. The study period is 5 years, with 2 years of enrolment.
primary_outcomes: Level of misunderstanding in clinician-patient conversations
title: Effective Communication in Perinatal Care

brief_summary: This prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled Phase II study is designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of romiplostim for platelet engraftment after haploidentical or HLA-matched unrelated donor allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Approximately 120 patients aged ≥18 years will be randomized equally to the romiplostim group or the best supportive care group. Romiplostim will be administered subcutaneously at 1 μg/kg once weekly, starting on day +3 after transplantation. The primary outcomes are platelet engraftment rates at days +30 after transplantation.
primary_outcomes: Platelet Engraftment Rate at Day +30 After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation
title: Romiplostim for Platelet Engraftment After Haploidentical or Matched Unrelated Donor Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation

brief_summary: ATLAS is a prospective, observational, multicenter cohort study of how accurately the Universal Cardiac Surgical Risk Score (UCSRS) predicts 30-day outcomes after adult cardiac surgery, compared head-to-head with two established models, STS-PROM and EuroSCORE II. Consecutive adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery are enrolled at each participating center over 12 months. All three scores are recorded for each patient. No score is returned to the treating team or influences clinical care. Discrimination and calibration of each score are assessed against 30-day major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). The model under evaluation, UCSRS version 3.2, was specified and calibrated against published registry mortality using simulated patients before enrollment. No simulated patient has an outcome, so no performance claim is made before this study.
primary_outcomes: 30 day MACCE
30 day all cause mortality
title: Assessment of Transnational Performance of the Universal Cardiac Surgical Risk Score Across International Sites

brief_summary:
This pilot study will examine whether adding virtual reality-based optokinetic stimulation to jump-landing training changes landing technique and inward knee movement in young adult athletes. Optokinetic stimulation involves watching moving visual scenes through a virtual reality headset.

Twenty licensed basketball or volleyball athletes aged 18-24 years will be randomly assigned to two groups. Both groups will complete the same jump-landing training, consisting of two blocks of 10 repetitions with performance feedback. One group will also receive seated virtual reality-based optokinetic stimulation before each training block.

Landing technique will be assessed using the Landing Error Scoring System. Inward knee movement will be assessed by measuring the frontal plane projection angle during single-leg squats. Assessments will take place before training, after training, and one week later to determine whether any changes are retained. The assessor will not know which group each participant has been assigned to.
primary_outcomes: Landing Error Scoring System (LESS) Score
title: Effects of Virtual Reality-Based Optokinetic Stimulation on Landing Technique and Dynamic Knee Valgus in Athletes

brief_summary:
In France, perinatal mental health has become a major public health issue. Maternal mental health conditions can have serious consequences, including death by suicide. Fathers may also experience significant psychological distress during the perinatal period. These difficulties can affect parents' well-being, the developing parent-infant relationship, and family life, highlighting the importance of early identification and appropriate support for both parents.

The birth of an infant before 28 completed weeks of gestation can be a traumatic experience for parents. Concerns about the infant's survival and health, together with the unfamiliar environment of a neonatal intensive care unit, can disrupt the transition to parenthood and may be associated with severe depressive symptoms and childbirth-related post-traumatic stress symptoms.

This single-centre observational study explores the psychological experiences of couples following the birth of an infant before 28 completed weeks of gestation. Its primary objective is to assess childbirth-related post-traumatic stress symptoms using the City Birth Trauma Scale. Secondary objectives are to assess depressive symptoms and explore parental representations, emotional experiences, and psychological functioning.

Couples will be invited to participate during their infant's hospitalisation in the neonatal intensive care unit at Besançon University Hospital, France. Both parents in each couple will participate, with individual assessments taking place at least one month after birth. Each assessment session will last approximately 90 minutes and will include a semi-structured interview using the Clinical Interview for Parents of High-Risk Infants (CLIP), the Rorschach test, and two self-report questionnaires: the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) and the City Birth Trauma Scale, using the appropriate maternal or partner version.

This exploratory study aims to improve understanding of parental psychological vulnerability following extremely preterm birth. In the longer term, its findings may raise healthcare professionals' awareness of maternal and paternal distress and inform approaches to systematic screening for postnatal depression and childbirth-related post-traumatic stress symptoms. Ultimately, this research seeks to support the development of care that addresses both parents' psychological needs and promotes early parent-infant relationships.
primary_outcomes: Childbirth related post-traumatic stress disorder
title: The Effects of Extreme Prematurity on Parenting

brief_summary:
This clinical trial will compare platelet-rich plasma (PRP)-assisted regenerative endodontic treatment with conventional root canal treatment in mature permanent teeth with pulp necrosis and apical periodontitis.

Ten participants will be included, and each participant will contribute two eligible single-rooted, single-canal teeth. Within each participant, one tooth will receive PRP-assisted regenerative endodontic treatment and the other tooth will receive conventional root canal treatment.

The primary objective is to compare radiographic periapical healing between the two treatments at 12 months. Secondary outcomes will include postoperative pain, analgesic use, clinical signs and symptoms, pulp sensibility, treatment success, tooth survival, and adverse events. Clinical and radiographic follow-up will be performed at 6, 12, and 24 months.
primary_outcomes: Percentage Reduction in Periapical Lesion Area
title: PRP-Assisted Regenerative Endodontics Versus Conventional Root Canal Treatment in Mature Necrotic Teeth

brief_summary:
\*\*Brief Summary\*\*

This assessor-blinded randomized clinical trial compared the analgesic effectiveness of longitudinal subcostal (QL-LS) and anterior (QL-A) quadratus lumborum blocks following cesarean section. Both approaches provided comparable pain control at rest and during movement. The QL-LS group demonstrated a significantly longer time to first rescue analgesia than the QL-A group (419.5 vs. 295.5 minutes; p \< 0.001), without a significant difference in 24-hour fentanyl consumption. Block performance times and adverse event profiles were similar. The prolonged initial analgesia with QL-LS may be associated with its more cranial injection site and potential differences in local anesthetic spread. These findings suggest that QL-LS prolongs the time to first rescue analgesia but does not demonstrate superiority in pain intensity reduction or overall opioid consumption.

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial aims to evaluate the efficacy of Capacitive and Resistive Energy Transfer (TECAR) therapy combined with an exercise program in patients with plantar fasciitis. The effects of active TECAR therapy will be compared with sham TECAR therapy, both combined with the same exercise program, in terms of pain intensity, functional status, and ultrasonographic plantar fascia thickness.

TECAR therapy is a non-invasive physical therapy modality used in musculoskeletal rehabilitation. Although it is increasingly used in clinical practice, evidence from sham-controlled randomized trials in patients with plantar fasciitis remains limited.

This study aims to determine whether active TECAR therapy provides additional benefits over sham treatment when combined with exercise. The findings are expected to contribute to the evidence regarding the clinical efficacy of TECAR therapy in the management of plantar fasciitis.

brief_summary:
1. Research background: Guided bone regeneration (GBR), as a bone augmentation technique, is widely used for the reconstruction of hard-tissue defects in implant dentistry. Terheyden classified bone defects into four types according to the spatial relationship between the defect and the intended implant site. Among these, type 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 are recommended to be managed with a staged protocol: bone augmentation first, followed by dental implant placement. The selection of barrier membranes for GBR depends on the size of the bone defect, and severe three-dimensional bone deficiencies require additional mechanical support. The digitally fabricated PEEK biological barrier is a product of the world's first digital PEEK bone augmentation system newly developed by Kangtuo Medical Group in 2026. It enables predictable bone gain and contour reconstruction, adapts to irregularly shaped bone defects, and provides complete cell exclusion as well as full soft-tissue isolation without the need for an overlying membrane. The system supports full-workflow planning and clinician-driven design. Being radiolucent, it facilitates sequential observation of bone remodeling, and the device is also easy to retrieve. Nevertheless, its clinical performance following GBR in severe bone defect sites remains to be further evaluated.
2. Research objective: To evaluate the bone stability and soft tissue healing outcomes following guided bone regeneration (GBR) using a digital PEEK biological barrier in sites with severe bone defects. This study aims to provide evidence based references for clinicians when selecting barrier membranes, so as to facilitate optimal clinical decision making for bone augmentation.
3. Study design and methods: Design type: multicentral prospective clinical study. Study duration: 3 years. Start time: From the date of adoption of ethics. End time: 2029. For all included patients, cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans and intraoral scans will be performed preoperatively, immediately postoperatively, and at 6-8 months postoperatively.
primary_outcomes: Bone augmentation
title: Clinical Efficacy Assessment of Digitally Fabricated PEEK Barrier Membranes for Guided Bone Regeneration in Severe Bone Defects

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the RAPID procedure works to treat colorectal cancer that has spread to the liver and cannot be removed by surgery. It will also learn about the safety of the procedure. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. How many participants are alive without the cancer progressing or returning 2 years after the first-stage surgery?
2. How many participants complete the second-stage surgery, and how quickly does the liver graft grow between the two stages?
3. What medical problems do participants have around the time of surgery, including serious complications?

Participants will:

1. Undergo the first-stage surgery: removal of the left part of the liver and implantation of a small liver graft, with the right portal vein tied off to help the graft grow;
2. Have blood tests and ultrasound checks after surgery, and regular CT or MRI scans to measure graft growth;

(4) Undergo the second-stage surgery to remove the remaining diseased liver once the graft has grown enough (5) Visit the clinic every 3 months for up to 2 years after the second-stage surgery for checkups, imaging, and blood tests to see if the cancer has returned
lead_sponsor: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
primary_outcomes: 2-Year Tumor Event-Free Survival Rate
title: RAPID for Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastases

brief_summary:
Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is the most common arrhythmia following cardiac surgery and is associated with increased risks of mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction, and hospital readmission. The cardiac autonomic nervous system plays an important role in the development of POAF and may represent a potential target for preventive intervention.

The CALM trial is a multicenter, randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of partial cardiac denervation for the prevention of POAF in patients undergoing isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). A total of approximately 1,470 participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo CABG with partial cardiac denervation or CABG alone. Partial cardiac denervation consists of transection of the ligament of Marshall and resection of the Waterston fat pad.

The trial will evaluate the incidence of POAF within the first 6 postoperative days and the occurrence of long-term adverse clinical events. Participants will undergo scheduled rhythm monitoring and clinical follow-up, and all participants will be followed until the last enrolled participant completes 3 years of follow-up after surgery.
lead_sponsor: China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation Within 6 Postoperative Days
Time to First Occurrence of the Composite Clinical Outcome
title: Partial Cardiac Denervation for Preventing Atrial Fibrillation After CABG

brief_summary:
Pain after root canal treatment is a common problem, particularly in teeth with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis, a condition involving severe inflammation of the tissue inside the tooth. Submucosal cryotherapy, which involves applying cold saline through an injection near the affected tooth, may help reduce postoperative pain and inflammation. Anti-inflammatory medications, such as diclofenac sodium and dexamethasone, may also provide pain relief.

This randomized clinical trial aims to evaluate the effects of submucosal cryotherapy, alone or combined with anti-inflammatory medications, on postoperative pain and interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels in patients undergoing root canal treatment of upper molars with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis.

A total of 90 adult patients will be randomly assigned to six groups: local anesthesia alone, cryotherapy with anesthesia, diclofenac sodium with anesthesia, dexamethasone with anesthesia, cryotherapy combined with diclofenac sodium, or cryotherapy combined with dexamethasone. All participants will undergo standardized single-visit root canal treatment.

Postoperative pain will be evaluated during the first 72 hours after treatment. IL-6, a substance involved in inflammation, will be measured in blood samples collected from the dental pulp during treatment. The need for additional pain medication and the occurrence of postoperative flare-ups will also be assessed.

The study seeks to determine whether combining submucosal cryotherapy with anti-inflammatory medications provides greater postoperative pain relief than individual interventions or standard care alone.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity Assessed Using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS)

brief_summary:
Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction complicates 0.1-3% of cardiac surgical procedures and is strongly associated with elevated postoperative mortality. Pulmonary hypertension is a key determinant of perioperative RV failure. Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is a selective pulmonary vasodilator that reduces pulmonary arterial pressure and has been widely used as adjunctive therapy in this setting. However, whether iNO influences systemic microcirculatory perfusion in these patients remains undefined.

We conducted a single-centre, prospective, interventional study. Adult patients with post-cardiotomy RV dysfunction - defined as central venous pressure (CVP) ≥ 15 mmHg combined with a pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) \> 35 mmHg on transthoracic echocardiography - were eligible. On top of standard postoperative care, patients received inhaled NO at 10-20 ppm for 2 hours without any concomitant change in vasoactive support. General characteristics, haemodynamic variables and sublingual microcirculatory parameters were recorded at baseline and again after 2 hours of iNO. The primary endpoint was the change in sublingual perfused vessel density (PVD). Secondary endpoints included mean arterial pressure (MAP), CVP, transthoracic echocardiographic indices, oxygenation index (OI), other sublingual microcirculatory parameters, capillary refill time (CRT), duration of mechanical ventilation and ICU length of stay.
primary_outcomes: perfused vessel density (PVD)
title: Effects of Inhaled Nitric Oxide on Sublingual Microcirculation in Patients With Right Ventricular Dysfunction After Cardiac Surgery

The more commonly adopted protocol consists of performing ECP procedures on two consecutive days every two weeks initially, and then once a month. The investigators hypothesized that a new ECP protocol consisting of one single apheresis procedure on day 1, processing 5000 ml of total blood volume (TBV), followed by product photo-irradiation and split into two equivalent aliquots to be administered on day 1 and 2, respectively, is safe and might improve self-reported QoL of cGVHD patients.

The goal of this observational study is to predict who will have problems after the breathing tube is removed. Taking out the tube is called extubation, and having these problems is called extubation failure. Participants are adults in the intensive care unit (ICU) who use a breathing machine (ventilator).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How well can computer tools predict problems in the 7 days after the tube is removed?
* Which information, such as age or blood tests, matters most for the prediction?

Extubation failure means the participant needs the tube put back in, needs a surgical opening in the neck to help breathing, or dies.

Researchers will use machine learning to build the computer tools. Machine learning is a type of artificial intelligence that finds patterns in data. Researchers will compare five types of machine learning to see which works best. They will build the tools with participants from Dr. Cipto Mangunkusumo National General Hospital in Jakarta. They will test the tools with participants from Universitas Indonesia Hospital in Depok.

Participants get their usual care. Doctors do not use the tools to make treatment decisions. Researchers will:

* Record health information about participants before the tube is removed
* Follow participants for 7 days after the tube is removed
primary_outcomes: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of machine learning models for predicting extubation failure
title: Predicting Extubation Failure Using Machine Learning

brief_summary:
Background and Objectives:

Medical professionals frequently work night shifts and rotating schedules. Night shift work, accompanied by sleep deprivation and stress, is a significant trigger for migraine attacks. Traditional preventive migraine medications usually require continuous administration and gradual dose titration, making them unsuitable for short-term, intermittent prevention specifically during night shifts. Rimegepant, a small-molecule CGRP receptor antagonist orally disintegrating tablet, has a rapid onset of action and a relatively short half-life, making it suitable for intermittent administration (i.e., situational prevention) prior to predictable periods of high migraine risk.

This study aims to evaluate whether administering Rimegepant 75 mg orally within 2 hours before the start of a night shift and at the end of the night shift can effectively prevent moderate-to-severe migraine during the night shift and the 24-hour post-shift observation window.

Study Design:

This is a prospective, open-label, randomized, two-cycle crossover clinical study conducted in China. Approximately 260 eligible participants are planned to be enrolled.

After a 4-week screening/baseline observation period, participants will be randomized 1:1 to one of two treatment sequences:

Sequence A: Rimegepant situational preventive treatment in Treatment Period 1, followed by a 10-day washout period, and standard care in Treatment Period 2.

Sequence B: Standard care in Treatment Period 1, followed by a 10-day washout period, and Rimegepant situational preventive treatment in Treatment Period 2.

Each treatment period lasts 4 weeks. Subsequently, all participants will enter a 4-week open-label extension period to receive Rimegepant treatment.

Target Population:

Study Population: Clinicians or nurses aged 18-60 working in Chinese hospitals.

Key Inclusion Criteria: Diagnosis of migraine (with or without aura) according to ICHD-3 criteria; at least 1 migraine attack occurring in the night-shift-related observation window per month over the past 3 months; at least 1 moderate-to-severe migraine attack during the 4-week screening period; ability to complete the electronic diary (eDiary).

Key Exclusion Criteria: Patients with chronic migraine; history of hepatic or renal impairment; history of hypersensitivity to CGRP receptor antagonists; participation in another clinical study within the past 3 months; pregnant or breastfeeding women, etc.

Primary Outcome Measures:

Primary Endpoint: The mean number of moderate-to-severe migraine days per evaluable night-shift-related observation window during each 4-week treatment period (assessed via eDiary).

Key Secondary Endpoints: Mean headache/migraine days within the night-shift-related observation window; number of moderate-to-severe migraine attacks during the night shift; days of acute migraine medication use; and changes in scale scores including sleep quality (PSQI), quality of life (MSQoL), and headache impact (HIT-6).

Significance:

The results of this study are expected to provide a feasible, effective, and targeted situational preventive strategy for migraine for medical professionals, a high-risk occupational population, and to provide clinical evidence for migraine management in similar short-term high-risk scenarios.
primary_outcomes: Mean number of moderate-to-severe migraine days per evaluable night-shift-related observation window
title: A Prospective Study of Rimegepant for Short-term Preventive Treatment of Night-shift-related Migraine in Healthcare Professionals

brief_summary: Over the past decades, advances in radiation therapy technology have significantly reduced treatment-related toxicity. To the best of our knowledge, no clinical studies have evaluated pLDRT in patients with DMG. Therefore, the primary objective of this phase I study is to evaluate the tolerability of pLDRT in this predominantly pediatric population and to determine a safe dose level for future clinical investigation.

brief_summary:
Gestational diabetes is a type of diabetes that develops during pregnancy and can increase the risk of health problems for both mothers and babies. Gestational diabetes is particularly common in American Samoa, where there is a need for effective approaches to prevent the condition and help pregnant women manage their blood sugar.

The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether a group prenatal care program called Strong Together Raising Our Next Generation (STRONG) can reduce the risk of developing gestational diabetes among pregnant women with overweight or obesity in American Samoa. The study will also examine whether additional group-based education and support can improve blood sugar control among women who develop gestational diabetes.

Researchers will enroll 360 pregnant women aged 18 years or older who are in their first 14 weeks of pregnancy. Participants will be randomly assigned (like flipping a coin) to receive either STRONG group prenatal care or usual individual prenatal care. STRONG combines routine prenatal care with group discussions, education about healthy eating and physical activity, goal setting, and peer support.

At 24-28 weeks of pregnancy, all participants will be screened for gestational diabetes. Women who do not develop gestational diabetes will continue with their assigned prenatal care. Women who develop gestational diabetes will be randomly assigned a second time to receive either additional group-based diabetes education or usual one-on-one diabetes counseling, alongside their ongoing prenatal care.

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

Does STRONG group prenatal care reduce the number of women who develop gestational diabetes compared with usual prenatal care?

Among women who develop gestational diabetes, which combination of prenatal care and diabetes education leads to better blood sugar control?

Researchers will also examine pregnancy and birth outcomes, infant health, and blood sugar levels after delivery. Participants will be followed until approximately six weeks after giving birth.

The findings may help identify effective, culturally appropriate ways to prevent and manage gestational diabetes in American Samoa and similar communities.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM)
Continuous Glucose Monitoring Time in Range at 30-32 Weeks
Continuous Glucose Monitoring Time in Range at 36-38 Weeks

brief_summary: Breast cancer is one of the most common malignancies among women worldwide, and surgery remains its primary treatment modality. Perioperative sleep disturbance, anxiety, depression, and acute postoperative pain are common complications in breast cancer patients. Among these, sleep disturbance is the most common and can exacerbate negative emotions and postoperative pain, delay postoperative recovery, and severely impair patients' psychological well-being and rehabilitation quality. Traditional benzodiazepine sedative-hypnotics are of limited use in the perioperative setting because of drawbacks such as drug dependence and withdrawal reactions. As a novel dual orexin receptor antagonist, lemborexant regulates sleep-wake balance, is non-addictive, and exhibits a superior safety profile. However, studies on its perioperative application in breast cancer patients remain scarce, and robust clinical evidence supporting its use is lacking. This prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial was designed primarily to investigate the efficacy of lemborexant in improving perioperative sleep quality in breast cancer patients, and secondarily to observe its effects on anxiety, depression, and acute postoperative pain, as well as to evaluate its safety profile. The findings of this study are expected to provide a safe and effective novel intervention strategy for the standardized perioperative management of sleep, mood, and pain in breast cancer patients, and to generate reliable evidence for optimizing enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) programs.
primary_outcomes: Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) total score
title: Lemborexant on Perioperative Sleep Quality in Patients Undergoing Breast Cancer Surgery

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate how accurately and quickly artificial intelligence (AI) can separate individual teeth from digital dental scans of adults with dental crowding. The study will compare AI-based tooth segmentation with manual segmentation performed by experienced orthodontists.

Digital dental scans from adult patients with moderate to severe dental crowding will be analyzed. The scans will be processed using two orthodontic software programs, Archform 2.6.4.1 and Blue Sky Plan V5, which use AI to automatically identify and separate individual teeth. The same scans will also be manually segmented by experienced orthodontists.

The study will compare the results from the different methods by assessing whether the teeth are correctly identified and separated, the accuracy of tooth measurements, the types of segmentation errors, and the time required to complete the segmentation.

The study aims to determine whether AI-based segmentation can provide accurate results while reducing the time required for digital orthodontic analysis. The findings may help improve the efficiency of digital orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning, particularly for adults with crowded teeth.

brief_summary:
Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is commonly used in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. A frequent complication of CRRT is a drop in blood pressure that requires treatment, known as CRRT-associated hemodynamic instability. This complication is linked to higher mortality and poorer kidney recovery.

The diastolic shock index (DSI) is a simple bedside measure calculated by dividing heart rate by diastolic blood pressure. It requires no additional devices, blood tests or invasive procedures, and higher values have been associated with vasopressor need and mortality in septic shock.

This prospective observational study aims to determine whether DSI measured before the start of CRRT can predict hemodynamic instability during CRRT in adult intensive care unit patients. The predictive performance of DSI will also be compared with the classic shock index, the modified shock index and mean arterial pressure. All data will be obtained from routine clinical monitoring; no additional intervention will be performed for the study.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Performance of Pre-CRRT Diastolic Shock Index for Predicting CRRT-Associated Hemodynamic Instability
title: Diastolic Shock Index for Predicting Hemodynamic Instability During Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy

brief_summary:
PRIDE Study - Brief Summary

The PRIDE Study (Prospective Research on Identification of Dementia in Early Stages) is a multicenter, prospective, observational study designed to estimate the prevalence of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) among adults aged 65 years and older reporting Subjective Memory Complaints (SMC), and to identify clinical, neuropsychological, functional, cardiovascular, metabolic, and lifestyle-related factors associated with cognitive decline and progression to clinically diagnosed dementia.

Subjective memory complaints are common in older adults and may represent an early manifestation of cognitive deterioration. However, not all individuals reporting memory difficulties have objective cognitive impairment, and the factors influencing progression to MCI or dementia remain incompletely understood.

The primary objective of the study is to determine the prevalence of MCI at baseline among individuals with SMC using standardized clinical and neuropsychological assessments.

Secondary objectives include evaluating the prevalence of subjective memory complaints, identifying factors associated with cognitive impairment, assessing longitudinal changes in cognitive performance, and investigating progression from subjective memory complaints to MCI and from MCI to clinically diagnosed dementia. The study will also assess participant retention, data completeness, and the reliability and reproducibility of the Memory Complaint Questionnaire (MAC-Q).

The study plans to recruit approximately 1,000 participants aged 65 years or older across participating healthcare centers. Eligible individuals must report subjective memory difficulties, provide valid informed consent, and be willing to undergo cognitive assessments and annual follow-up evaluations.

At baseline, participants will undergo standardized assessments covering sociodemographic characteristics, medical history, comorbidities, cardiovascular and metabolic risk factors, functional status, lifestyle characteristics, and cognitive performance.

Participants will be followed for five years, with annual evaluations at 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 months. Changes in cognitive function and the occurrence of clinically diagnosed MCI or dementia will be documented throughout follow-up.

Cognitive screening findings will be distinguished from formal clinical diagnoses. When clinically indicated, participants may undergo specialist evaluation through routine healthcare pathways. Diagnoses of dementia will be recorded only when clinically established and documented.

This is a non-interventional study. No experimental treatments, randomization, or modifications to routine clinical care are planned.

The PRIDE Study aims to improve understanding of early cognitive decline and identify factors associated with progression toward dementia, providing evidence to support risk stratification, early recognition, and future preventive strategies in older adults.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of Mild Cognitive Impairment at Baseline
Prevalence of Mild Cognitive Impairment Among Older Adults With Subjective Memory Complaints
title: Prospective Research on Identification of Dementia in Early Stages (P.R.I.D.E)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to find out whether a phenotype-based pain management approach can reduce chronic pain in adults (18 years and older) who have completed curative treatment for head and neck cancer and continue to experience chronic post-treatment pain.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a phenotype-based pain management approach reduce participants' average pain by at least 75% after one month of treatment?
* Is the treatment safe, with 10% or fewer participants stopping treatment because of side effects?

Participants will:

* Attend three study visits over one month (at baseline, 2 weeks, and 4 weeks).
* Complete questionnaires about their pain, anxiety, depression, medication side effects, and use of pain medicines.
* Undergo a detailed examination to identify the type (phenotype) of their pain.
* Receive a treatment plan tailored to their pain phenotype, which may include medications, trigger point injections, or nerve blocks, depending on their symptoms and pain severity.
* Return for follow-up visits to assess pain relief, medication side effects, and use of breakthrough pain medication.
lead_sponsor: Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital & Research Centre
primary_outcomes: Pain Reduction
title: Phenotype-based Model for Managing Chronic Post-treatment Pain Among Head and Neck Cancer Survivors: a Pilot Study

brief_summary: This is an multicenter, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial. Adult patients (14-65 years) with acute lymphoblastic leukemia in second complete remission (CR2) scheduled for allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) will be randomized 1:1 to receive either busulfan-based chemotherapy-only conditioning (experimental arm) or total-body-irradiation (TBI)-based conditioning (active comparator arm). The primary objective is to test the non-inferiority of chemotherapy-based conditioning versus TBI-based conditioning regarding 1-year leukemia-free survival (LFS). Secondary endpoints include treatment-related mortality (TRM), cumulative incidence of relapse (CIR), graft-versus-host-disease (GVHD), and overall survival (OS). All patients receive uniform GVHD prophylaxis and post-transplant supportive care.
primary_outcomes: 1-Year Leukemia-Free Survival (LFS)
title: Busulfan-Based Versus TBI-Based Conditioning for Adult ALL-CR2 Allo-HSCT

brief_summary:
The goal of this interventional study is to learn if slump neural tensioner and slump neural slider techniques can immediately improve dynamic balance in asymptomatic healthy young adults aged 18-25 years. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the slump neural tensioner technique produce greater immediate improvement in dynamic balance compared to the slump neural slider technique? Do both techniques improve Y Balance Test scores immediately after a single session of treatment?

Researchers will compare the slump neural tensioner group to the slump neural slider group to see if one technique produces a greater immediate effect on dynamic balance.

Participants will:

Be randomly assigned to receive either the slump neural slider or the slump neural tensioner technique in a single session Perform 10 repetitions of their assigned technique for 3 sets in the slump sitting position Have their dynamic balance measured using the Lower Quarter Y Balance Test before and immediately after the intervention Complete the entire session in approximately 30-45 minutes in one visit only
conditions: Dynamic Balance in Asymptomatic Young Adults
primary_outcomes: Change in normalized Y-Balance Test composite scores from baseline to immediately and 20 min after intervention
title: Immediate Effect of Slump Neural Tensioners Compared With Neural Sliders on Dynamic Balance in Asymptomatic Young Adults

brief_summary: This study aims to determine whether an abbreviated course of thoracic radiotherapy, delivered in five fractions over one week between chemotherapy cycles, improves progression-free survival compared with standard radiotherapy delivered concurrently with chemotherapy in patients with newly diagnosed limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC).
lead_sponsor: London Health Sciences Centre Research Institute OR Lawson Research Institute of St. Joseph's
primary_outcomes: Progression-free survival
title: A Randomized Trial of Standard vs. Hypofractionated Accelerated Radiotherapy for Progression in Limited-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
This prospective, randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness of kinesio taping as an adjunct to standard conservative treatment in women with stage II lower-extremity lipedema.

A total of 30 women will be randomly assigned to two groups: a control group receiving standard conservative treatment and an intervention group receiving kinesio taping in addition to standard conservative treatment. Both groups will receive patient education, physical activity recommendations, and a standardized home exercise program. The intervention group will additionally receive bilateral lower-extremity kinesio taping twice weekly for six weeks.

Participants will be assessed at baseline, week 6 (end of treatment), and week 10 (four-week follow-up). The primary outcome will be the change in pain intensity measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at week 6. Secondary outcomes will include lower-extremity functional status (LEFS), quality of life (EQ-5D-3L), walking performance (4-meter walk test), lower-extremity circumference measurements, and pressure pain threshold assessed using an algometer.

The study aims to determine whether adding kinesio taping to standard conservative treatment provides additional clinical benefits in women with lipedema.
primary_outcomes: Change in Pain Intensity Measured by the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: Effectiveness of Kinesio Taping as an Adjunct to Conservative Treatment in Women With Lipedema

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to find out which of three standard skin care approaches works best to prevent a skin reaction called radiation dermatitis (redness, irritation, or breakdown of the skin) in people receiving radiation therapy after mastectomy.
primary_outcomes: Rate of acute radiation dermatitis with most desquamation (ARD-MD)
title: A Study of Different Skin Care Approaches to Prevent Skin Reactions in People With Breast Cancer Receiving Radiation Therapy After Mastectomy

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial will compare an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted teleglaucoma referral pathway with conventional referral among adults identified with referable glaucoma through the Los Angeles County Department of Health Services (LAC DHS) Teleretinal Screening Program. The primary objective is to determine whether AI-assisted referral reduces time to in-office diagnosis of manifest glaucoma. Secondary outcomes include glaucoma severity, visual function, need for glaucoma surgery, patient-reported quality of life and satisfaction, health system resource utilization, and cost-effectiveness.
primary_outcomes: Time to in-office diagnosis of glaucoma
title: AI-Assisted vs Conventional Teleglaucoma Referral

brief_summary:
Nail psoriasis can change how your nails look and cause pain, making everyday activities uncomfortable and affecting your confidence. Treatments include creams or ointments, injections, medicines that work throughout the body, and laser therapy. The choice depends on your age, symptoms, overall health, preferences, and possible side effects.

Steroid injections can help, but they may be painful and can cause bruising under the nail or thinning of the skin around the injection site. Fractional CO2 laser creates tiny channels in the nail to help medicines applied to it pass through more easily. Studies have reported improvement with laser treatment, although adding certain ointments has not always worked better than laser alone.

Tacrolimus 0.1% ointment has also shown promising results. The proposed study aims to find out whether combining this ointment with fractional CO2 laser works better than using the ointment alone.
primary_outcomes: the improvement of the Target Nail Psoriasis Severity Index (tNAPSI) score before and after treatment
title: Efficacy of Fractional Co2 Laser With Topical Tacrolimus 0.1 in the Treatment of Nail Psoriasis

brief_summary: This is a randomized, single-center phase 2 study comparing early versus delayed oral feeding after total laryngectomy. Dysphagia-related outcomes will be assessed using the MDADI preoperatively, and on postoperative days 14 (±7) and 30 (±7). Secondary outcomes include fistula requiring intervention, surgical site infection, wound dehiscence, oral feeding tolerance, feeding tube duration, nasogastric tube removal, length of stay, PSS-HN scores, and patient-reported oral rehabilitation.
primary_outcomes: Early oral feeding versus delayed oral feeding.
MD Anderson Dysphagia Inventory (MDADI) total score
Summary measure
title: Early Feeding TL Trial

brief_summary:
This prospective, randomized controlled trial aims to compare two methods of tracheal extubation after general anesthesia in adults with morbid obesity undergoing elective laparoscopic surgery.

A total of 120 patients will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. In the first group, the breathing tube will be removed while the patient remains deeply anesthetized, followed immediately by heated and humidified high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO). Patients will then be allowed to awaken without unnecessary stimulation. In the second group, the breathing tube will be removed after the patient is fully awake, followed by conventional oxygen therapy through a face mask.

The primary objective is to determine whether HFNO-assisted deep extubation reduces the incidence of coughing during the first 15 minutes after extubation compared with conventional awake extubation.

The study will also assess respiratory complications, the need for airway interventions, hemodynamic changes, recovery times, and adverse events associated with the two extubation approaches.

The findings may help inform airway management strategies during recovery from general anesthesia in patients with morbid obesity.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Coughing During Extubation and Early Emergence
title: High-Flow Nasal Oxygen-Assisted Deep Extubation Versus Awake Extubation in Morbidly Obese Patients

brief_summary: An observational study combines retrospective and prospective cohorts to develop, validate, and compare models based on Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-related blood biomarkers alone, nasopharyngeal endoscopic scores alone, and their combination to support biopsy decisions for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Existing clinical data will be analyzed retrospectively for model development and internal validation. Data from participants undergoing nasopharyngeal endoscopy and clinically indicated nasopharyngeal biopsy at participating centers will be collected prospectively for external validation. The study will assess the models' diagnostic performance and potential value in identifying individuals who may benefit from biopsy and reducing unnecessary biopsies. Clinical decisions will follow routine practice.
interventions: Assessment of EBV-related blood biomarkers and nasopharyngeal endoscopic scores
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity of serological, endoscopic, and combined models at prespecified risk thresholds
Specificity of serological, endoscopic, and combined models at prespecified risk thresholds
title: Development and Validation of a Biopsy Decision Model for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Based on Serological Markers and Endoscopic Features

brief_summary: This prospective single-center study evaluated whether 4 weeks of phase-1 complex decongestive therapy (manual lymphatic drainage, multilayer short-stretch bandaging, decongestive exercise, and skin care) changes dermal and subcutaneous tissue thickness measured by high-frequency ultrasonography in adults with unilateral International Society of Lymphology stage 1-2 lower-limb lymphedema. Measurements were made at suprapatellar and infrapatellar sites of both limbs before and after treatment; the unaffected limb served as an internal control and body weight was recorded to distinguish local tissue change from systemic weight change.
primary_outcomes: Change in subcutaneous tissue thickness of the affected limb at the suprapatellar site
title: Ultrasonographic Tissue Thickness After Complex Decongestive Therapy in Lower-Limb Lymphedema

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of pelvic floor muscle training and a modified lumbopelvic belt on pain, kinesiophobia, and functional status in pregnant women with symphysis pubis pain.Although the power analysis yielded a relatively small minimum sample size, the target sample size was increased to account for potential loss to follow-up and missing data, as may occur in clinical research. brief_summary:
The effectiveness of discision in accelerating orthodontic canine retraction will be evaluated during clear aligner therapy and during conventional fixed orthodontic appliances.

Furthermore, the effectiveness of clear aligner therapy in achieving orthodontic canine retraction will be assessed.
primary_outcomes: Evaluation of maxillary canine retraction rate in millimeters per week
title: Discision as Acceleration Method in Canine Retraction in Orthodontics With Aligner and Fixed Appliances in Young Adults a Split Mouth Study

brief_summary:
A single-center, retrospective, observational study without experimental intervention, conducted at the Center of Excellence for Metabolic Health at IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital.

The primary objective of the study is to estimate the prevalence of dyslipidemia and evaluate its association with metabolic health status in overweight or obese subjects. Secondary objectives include characterizing cardiovascular risk; evaluating lipid, glycemic, and inflammatory profiles; analyzing longitudinal changes in these parameters during follow-up (where available); assessing the achievement of therapeutic targets recommended by ESC/EAS guidelines; and identifying predictors of metabolic response.

Approximately 900 patients are expected to be included, all enrolled at the Center of Excellence for Metabolic Health at IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital. Therefore, the total number of patients corresponds to that of the participating center.
primary_outcomes: To estimate the prevalence of dyslipidemia and assess its association with metabolic health in adults with overweight or obesity.
title: Impact of Dyslipidemia on Metabolic Health of Adults With Overweight/Obesity (IDOM): A Study at the San Raffaele Hospital Center for Metabolic Health

brief_summary: This is a single-center prospective clinical study in the intensive care unit (ICU). Thirty adult patients with sepsis requiring hemodynamic monitoring and fluid resuscitation will be enrolled. All participants will undergo two hemodynamic monitoring modalities simultaneously: pulse indicator continuous cardiac output (PiCCO) (reference standard) and arterial pulse contour cardiac output (APCO, ultrasound-calibrated pulse-contour cardiac output). The study aims to evaluate the consistency of clinical decision-making for fluid resuscitation guided by APCO compared with PiCCO, and to verify the accuracy of cardiac output (CO) measured by APCO. No investigational drugs will be administered. A standardized fluid challenge will be performed based on clinical indications. Hemodynamic parameters, laboratory results, and adverse events will be collected throughout the ICU stay.
lead_sponsor: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Agreement in fluid resuscitation decision-making between PiCCO and APCO
title: Ultrasound-Calibrated Pulse Contour Cardiac Output Monitoring: Value and Accuracy in Hemodynamic Care
